docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Cerebras earns from wafer-scale systems, hardware, cloud capacity, and related services for fast training/inference. It is a rare non-GPU public name, but technical scarcity comes with customer concentration, project financing, data-center leases, and losses. Revenue growth is proven; durable economics are not.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: CBRS is an alternative accelerator/system architecture in Semiconductors and Foundational Compute. TSMC fabricates WSE, so wafer realization remains in Semiconductor Manufacturing, Advanced Packaging, Test, and Materials. Selling cloud/service capacity does not make Cerebras a hyperscale demand owner.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: Customers buy systems/hardware or consume cloud/service compute. OpenAI/AWS relationships may expand deployment and distribution, but value capture depends on MW going live, utilization, gross margin, customer diversification, leases/capex, and financing terms.

docs.title: 2026-08-12 Q2 update (historical disclosure; current framing is updated by the 2026-10-04 delta)
docs.text:
• Q2 2026 revenue was USD 224.9M, up 87% year over year; core revenue was USD 216.0M and cloud revenue was USD 107.1M.
  • GAAP gross margin was 44.3% and GAAP net loss was USD 25.6M. The company raised full-year core-revenue outlook to USD 880M-890M, while concentration, utilization, financing, and capital intensity remain open.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Q1 2026 GAAP revenue was USD 193.406M, up 94%; cloud and other services revenue was USD 82.813M, up 178%.

  • GAAP gross margin was about 44.6%; GAAP operating loss was USD 15.037M.

  • Cerebras disclosed an OpenAI multi-year deal exceeding USD 20B / 750MW and an AWS partnership; Customer A/B were still 63%/11% of Q1 revenue.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text: • Prior FY2026 core revenue guidance was USD 855-865M, with core operating-margin guidance of (28)%-(32)%. The August 12 Q2 update raised revenue guidance to USD 880M-890M; the local Q2 capture does not update that historical operating-margin guide, and the older revenue range is superseded. The OpenAI/AWS relationships and wafer-scale inference path are presented as large-scale low-latency deployment. Contract disclosure does not prove deployment cadence, utilization, or margin.

docs.title: Reasonable inference

docs.title: CEG — Constellation Energy
docs.text: Role: Phase 5 E7 spine 7 generation / grid / time-to-power; CEG owns nuclear generation and contracted data-center power Structural status: core Formal discovery state: Market-found Evidence through: 2026-08-06

docs.title: 2026-08-06 Q2 earnings update
docs.text:
• Adjusted operating-EPS guidance rose to $11.50-$12.50, while Crane received the FERC CIR-transfer waiver and NRC fuel-license approval.
  • The company also signed 920 MW of additional long-term clean/reliable generation PPAs; Calpine integration and contract economics still need validation.

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Constellation is a large competitive power platform built on nuclear generation. After Calpine, it combines the largest nuclear fleet in the U.S. with complementary gas, geothermal, and storage assets plus a retail/commercial power platform.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: Within Power Generation, Grid, and Fuel Supply, CEG primary-owns nuclear generation and contracted data-center power. It owns the nuclear and flexible-power fleet, commercial electricity supply, and long-duration contracted power relationships. Its ownership stops at the site / utility handoff; inside-the-fence electrical distribution, cooling, EPC, and server / network layers do not belong here.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: AI load first becomes long-term power demand, then shows up in CEG's nuclear output, capacity, clean attributes, and commercial contracting capability. For data centers, revenue can come from existing nuclear supply or site-level contracted power arrangements such as Freestone. The monetized product is electricity and contracted power delivery, not the data-center's internal electrical system.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• The 2025 10-K disclosed that after the 2026-01-07 Calpine close, CEG had about 55 GW of generation capacity, including about 22 GW of nuclear capacity across 25 units, and served about 2.5M customer accounts.
  • The 10-K disclosed a 20-year Microsoft PPA supporting the restart of Crane Clean Energy Center.
  • Q1 2026 results also disclosed 44,666 GWh of nuclear generation in the quarter, a 92.3% owned nuclear capacity factor, and no non-refueling outage days at operated sites.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• The company expects Crane to provide about 835 MW of emissions-free capacity once restarted; restart still depends on regulatory approvals, interconnection-related construction, licensing, and execution timing.
  • Q1 2026 results disclosed that PUCT approved the net-metering application for the Freestone / CyrusOne data-center co-location arrangement, subject to conditions; the company also cited an existing 380 MW agreement and an additional 380 MW Phase 2 exclusive agreement.
  • Management frames the combined Calpine + nuclear platform as positioned to serve data centers, advanced manufacturing, and critical infrastructure with clean, reliable, and flexible power.
  • The Freestone data-center setup remains explicitly conditional.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• CEG's distinct ownership is not just "it has nuclear." It combines existing nuclear baseload, Calpine's flexible power fleet, and a commercial contracting platform into a long-duration contracted power offering.
  • That still does not make all nuclear, retail, or Calpine revenue AI revenue. AI monetization should appear first in specific contracts and sites.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• The actual Crane restart schedule, the full Phase 2 Freestone buildout, and the eventual share of CEG earnings tied to data-center contracts are not yet proven by reported results.
  • The platform's full clean-power revenue base should not be broadly extrapolated into AI monetization.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• The Microsoft / Crane contract path or restart path fails in a material way.
  • The Freestone approval, contracting, or actual delivery path breaks down.
  • Nuclear fleet reliability, capacity factors, or effective operating life deteriorate enough to weaken long-duration power delivery.
  • Calpine integration fails to strengthen, and instead weakens, CEG's ability to serve large-load contracted power demand.

docs.title: 2026-10-04 frozen decision
docs.text:
Classification: Group 2 — reopen only after the stated valuation and operating conditions; no current add.

Raised Q2 guidance, Crane regulatory progress and 920MW PPAs are operating proof; Calpine integration, secondary issuance, Crane/Freestone execution and same-date valuation still require review, exclusively through the VST/CEG/TLN SOT. Conditional watch.

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Celestica is a manufacturing, design, supply-chain, and platform-solutions company organized into CCS and ATS. For spine 6, the relevant segment is CCS, especially HPS: enterprise data communications, servers and storage, routers, switches, data center interconnects, and related platform design/manufacturing.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: In spine 6, CLS is a manufacturing/integration exposure. It is not a branded systems vendor, and it should not be lazily flattened into "just another ODM/EMS." It sits closer to hyperscaler data-center hardware, switching platforms, and complex platform delivery, but its boundary remains manufacturing, engineering, and delivery rather than end-product brand control.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text:
• Q1 FY2026 revenue was USD 4.05B, up 53% year over year; within that, CCS revenue was USD 3.24B, up 76%, with CCS margin of 8.6%.
  • In the same quarter, HPS revenue was about USD 1.7B, up 63% year over year.
  • Q4 2025 disclosed HPS revenue of about USD 1.4B, up 72% year over year; the company also disclosed U.S. capacity expansion supporting Google TPU systems and a third hyperscaler 1.6T switching platform program.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• The annual report defines CCS as the communications and enterprise (servers and storage) business and explicitly says its products can include routers, switches, data center interconnects, servers, and storage-related products.
  • Q1 FY2026 disclosed USD 3.24B of CCS revenue, USD 1.7B of HPS revenue, and the related growth and margin profile.
  • The Q4 2025 release disclosed that Celestica is Google's preferred manufacturing partner for data center hardware and systems and that it won a third hyperscaler 1.6T switching platform design-and-manufacturing program.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• The prior FY2026 revenue/adjusted-EPS outlook of USD 19.0B / 10.15 is superseded by the Q2 update to USD 20.5B / 11.30 above. The stronger 2027 visibility remains forward-looking.
  • The Google TPU U.S. expansion and 2027 ramp timing are roadmap statements, not completed outcomes.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• CLS fits better as a hyperscaler AI data-center hardware manufacturing and delivery partner than as a generic EMS discount case.
  • But it monetizes AI mainly through platform manufacturing, engineering, and delivery, not through the brand or final-system pricing power of a branded systems vendor.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• How much of CCS/HPS revenue can be strictly attributed to AI rather than broader cloud or networking refresh.
  • The duration, unit economics, and margin structure of each hyperscaler program.
  • The long-run margin lift to consolidated results from Google, 1.6T switching, and co-packaged-optics programs.

docs.title: COHR — Coherent
docs.text: Role: spine 4 multi-technology pluggable optics / photonics platform Structural status: core Formal discovery state: Market-found Evidence through: 2026-08-12

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Coherent is fundamentally a photonics platform company selling the technology routes and building blocks behind faster pluggable optics. Based on current local sources, the durable conclusion is not that every AI optical layer is already fully monetized, but that Coherent has real product and technology coverage across 1.6T, 3.2T, and further-out pluggable architectures.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: COHR primary-owns the photonics / pluggable-optics node in AI Interconnect, Optical Networking, and DCI. Current local sources clearly prove SiPh, InP, VCSEL, EML, laser, and modulator capability tied to 1.6T, 3.2T, and higher-speed pluggables; they do not prove switch-system ownership, and they do not quantify older-page claims around DCI, OCS, or broader platform revenue.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: As AI data centers move toward higher lane rates, denser pluggable optics, and multiple optical architectures coexisting, Coherent can increase content through lasers, EMLs, silicon-photonics PICs, VCSELs, and related pluggable building blocks. Profit will depend on design wins, manufacturing execution, yields, and product mix rather than demo breadth alone.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• The same source explicitly describes the company’s multi-technology platform strategy as Silicon Photonics, Indium Phosphide, and VCSEL-based solutions.
  • Named 1.6T transceiver technologies include a silicon-photonics PIC, a high-power InP CW laser, 200G InP EML, and 200G GaAs VCSEL.
  • The company also showed 400G/lane PAM4 optical links for 3.2T transceivers based on both 400G Differential EML and a pure-silicon PN-junction Mach-Zender Modulator.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• The 2026-03-17 OFC release says Coherent will showcase next-generation pluggable technologies spanning 1.6T, 3.2T, and architectures for 12.8T and beyond; this is product-release framing, not a realized commercial result.
  • The company says these demonstrations represent scalable, power-efficient connectivity for AI-driven data-center infrastructure.
  • Management says AI infrastructure is accelerating the transition to higher-speed pluggable architectures and positions XPO and related platforms as a path toward 12.8T and beyond.
  • Broader DCI, OCS, and platform-scale claims from the older page are not newly quantified in current local sources, so they remain directional rather than proven here.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: If higher-speed pluggable optics continue to use multiple optical approaches in parallel, Coherent’s multi-technology platform can reduce dependence on any single architecture and help it stay inside the upgrade cycle.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• Current local sources do not prove how much of company revenue or profit already comes from AI optics.
  • Current local sources do not prove that older-page DCI, OCS, or cross-campus interconnect claims have already become clear financial pillars.
  • Two linked PDF sources are only local stubs, so this page does not treat any uninspected debt, integration, or broader product detail as verified fact.

docs.text:

COHR’s FY2026 USD7.118bn revenue moves data-center demand into company-level financial evidence, but debt, working capital, awards, and collections after expansion still determine incremental capital returns. The 9.27x FY2026-sales screen permits only a conditional view: the next period must prove data-center gross margin and CFO after capex, not merely demand or capacity announcements.

This round’s economic classification is Group 2 (consider an addition only after the stated operating and valuation conditions close). This page adds no price band, sizing, or execution trigger; What Is Worth Buying owns the four-group judgment and 大仓确认：NO remains in force.

docs.title: CRDO — Credo Technology
docs.text: Role: spine 4 AEC / optical DSP / retimer connectivity-layer supplier Structural status: core Formal discovery state: Market-found Evidence through: 2026-09-02; action SOT: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger (registry row=none)

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Credo monetizes high-speed connectivity chips, AECs, optical/copper interconnect DSPs, and related IP. AI clusters turn bandwidth, power, and link stability into hard constraints, and Credo’s value is to make those short- and mid-reach links faster, more reliable, and more power-efficient.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: CRDO primary-owns the AI scale-out connectivity layer in AI Interconnect, Optical Networking, and DCI, especially AECs, retimers, optical/copper DSPs, and related connectivity solutions. It does not primary-own switch ASICs, GPUs, or full systems; this page is about the high-speed layer that links nodes together rather than the compute silicon itself.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: As hyperscalers and AI clusters move from 400G / 800G toward 1.6T, PCIe expansion, and higher port density, Credo can increase content per link and shipment volume through AECs, DSPs, retimers, connectivity ICs, and related IP. Profit depends on design wins, customer ramps, product mix, and whether power/reliability advantages convert into large-scale deployments.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• The company describes itself as a high-speed connectivity supplier for AI, cloud computing, and hyperscale networks, with product families that include ICs, AECs, SerDes chiplets, and SerDes IP licensing.
  • FY2026 Q4 revenue was USD 437.0M, up 157% YoY and 7.4% QoQ; GAAP / non-GAAP gross margin was 68.2% / 68.3%.
  • FY2026 revenue was USD 1.335B, versus USD 436.8M in FY2025; Q4 GAAP / non-GAAP net income was USD 169.1M / 226.7M.
  • Cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments were approximately USD 1.4B.
  • The DustPhotonics acquisition is complete, bringing silicon-photonics PIC capability in-house. Completion does not prove optical revenue or integration economics.
  • Named OFC 2026 products included 400G / 800G ZeroFlap optical transceivers, a 1.6T LRO module with Bluebird DSP, Gen6 PCIe over ZeroFlap AECs, and 1.6T ZeroFlap AECs.
  • Q1 FY2027 revenue was USD 479.0M, up 114.7% year over year and 9.6% sequentially, above the old USD 465M-475M guide; GAAP / non-GAAP gross margin was 64.5% / 68.0%. GAAP gross margin was 240bp below the old guide's lower bound, while non-GAAP gross margin landed at the old guide's midpoint, so the topline beat was not a margin-quality beat.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• Q2 FY2027 guidance is revenue USD 525M-535M, with GAAP / non-GAAP gross margin of 62.9%-64.9% / 67%-69%.
  • The company says its portfolio addresses optical/copper Ethernet and PCIe connectivity up to 1.6T, and positions ZeroFlap optics, optical DSPs, OmniConnect memory solutions, retimers, and DSPs as part of the AI infrastructure stack.
  • Management expects DustPhotonics to contribute growth in FY2027 and frames it as expansion across 800G / 1.6T / 3.2T NPO / CPO optical interconnect; the future contribution remains an issuer claim.
  • On the Q1 call, management said it had recognized first DustPhotonics silicon-photonics PIC revenue, with initial 800G / 1.6T wins ramping in FY2027, and reiterated a FY2027 optical-revenue target above USD 600M. This is a CALL-ONLY management claim captured through a secondary transcript.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: If AI networking continues to demand higher lane speeds, lower power, and more stable short-reach / rack-to-rack connectivity, Credo can raise value per link through AECs, DSPs, and retimers without being the switch-silicon vendor.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• First DustPhotonics PIC revenue proves only that the ramp has begun; current local sources still lack a filed breakdown of its scale, margin, or return economics.
  • Current sources also do not prove that hyperscaler demand will remain linear, or that Credo will keep the same share through every speed transition.
  • Q1 top-four end-customer concentration was 33% / 28% / 13% / 10% according to the call; diversification remains an open risk, not a closed gate.
  • This page does not prove system-layer economics outside Credo’s products, such as switch, NIC, or GPU platform ownership.

docs.title: Operating and capital delta as of 2026-10-04
docs.text:
This section supersedes older “current/latest” framing. Reported results and management guidance not yet replaced by results remain period evidence and testable gates; an August issuance date alone does not make a still-future guide obsolete.

Do not restate concentration, design wins, or optical architecture demand as revenue; the next period’s revenue/margin/cash is the test of price sustainability.

This round’s economic classification is Group 3 (not worth adding now). This page adds no price band, sizing, or execution trigger; What Is Worth Buying owns the four-group judgment and 大仓确认：NO remains in force.

Q1 FY2027 revenue cleared the old guide, Q2 guidance stepped higher, and first DustPhotonics PIC revenue appeared; however, GAAP gross margin missed the old guide, top-four concentration remains high, and filed optical economics are not broken out. docs.title: CRM — Salesforce
docs.text: Action route: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger selects Enterprise Software Platform Current-Live Two-Batch Writeback Ledger as CRM's sole current SOT; this entity carries no price bands, position sizing, or trade instruction.

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Salesforce turns deployed compute into enterprise application consumption across customer workflows, governed data, and agent execution. Data Cloud provides context and Agentforce provides reasoning and action, so the key question is not broad CRM revenue but whether those layers keep converting into billable seats, ARR, and usage.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text:
• Lane: E9 AI Application Production and Data Lifecycle enterprise application / platform consumption owner, centered on CRM, Data Cloud, and Agentforce monetization.
  • Boundary: it owns customer objects, governed context, and agent action. It does not own E2 compute silicon, E6 systems manufacturing/integration, or any E7/E8 power and facility layer.
  • Distinction: CRM's strength is customer-data and agent control-plane ownership, not generic cloud infrastructure and not pure workflow ticketing.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text:
• Customer 360 seats and workflows remain recurring revenue.
  • Data Cloud connects structured and unstructured enterprise context to the activation layer and can lift ARPU and attach.
  • Agentforce can convert AI into contracts and revenue through premium SKUs, agent usage, and flex-credit-like consumption, but broad revenue, subscription revenue, and AI + Data ARR are not the same as pure AI revenue.

docs.title: 2026-08-26 Q2 FY2027 update
docs.text:
• Q2 FY2027 revenue was USD 11.345B, up 11% year over year; cRPO was USD 33.5B, up 14%, and total RPO was USD 66.3B, up 11%.
  • Agentforce and Data 360 ARR reached nearly USD 3.9B, and Agentforce ARR exceeded USD 1.5B. Informatica contributed USD 456M of revenue, so the disclosed application measures do not establish a clean organic AI-revenue bridge.

docs.title: Acquisitions, cash and shares — 2026-10-04
docs.text:
• The correct USD 200M net FY27 revenue-guidance increase is USD 100M organic plus USD 200M Contentful / Fin less USD 100M FX. Contentful closed September 1 and Fin September 10; future standalone contribution and purchase accounting are not inferred.
  • H1 OCF of USD 7.970B less cash capex of USD 0.316B gives USD 7.654B; repurchase cash was USD 27.332B and net debt-issuance proceeds USD 24.842B. Cash/marketable securities of USD 11.403B and non-current debt of USD 39.288B remain separate; debt-funded repurchases are not operating-cash growth.
  • The USD 25B ASR cash payment and roughly 103m initial shares are executed, but final settlement is not. Investor Day's final average-price, share-reduction and return framework is management expectation, not realized investor return. Contentful / Fin assumed-award S-8 registrations are potential capacity, not already-issued shares.
  • The September Investor Day said the 14% Q3 cRPO growth guide excludes Contentful / Fin. Selected high-AWU customers' ARR uplift is correlation, not causal incremental AI revenue. Test organic renewal, contract profit and post-financing per-share cash; whole-business value need not depend on a separately disclosed AI revenue line.

Only the existing selected SOT owns actions; this entity creates no bands or sizing. Large-position confirmation: NO.

docs.title: Historical Q1 evidence ladder — not a substitute for Q2 and subsequent events above
Proven
docs.text:
• Q1 FY2027 revenue was USD 11.133B, up 13.27%.
  • Subscription and support revenue was USD 10.593B, up 13.94%.
  • cRPO was USD 33.6B, up 14%.
  • Total RPO was USD 67.9B, up 11%.
  • In the 10-Q subscription buckets, Agentforce Apps was USD 6.910B, up 8.91%, while Data 360 / Headless / Other was USD 3.683B, up 24.76%; the latter includes Informatica contribution.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• Agentforce ARR was about USD 1.2B, up 205%.
  • AI + Data ARR was nearly USD 3.4B, including about USD 1.1B of Informatica Cloud ARR.
  • Agentic Work Units reached 3.8B cumulatively and are management's clearest current proof of agent activity.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• If Data Cloud's governed context and Agentforce's action layer keep lifting attach and renewals, CRM can move AI from feature enhancement into application-layer platform monetization.
  • The Slack / MCP / Flow stack makes CRM closer to an enterprise agent control plane than to a simple seat-software suite.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• There is still no clean dollar bridge from paid Agentforce consumption to reported revenue.
  • AI + Data ARR is not a pure organic AI metric and cannot be extrapolated directly into durable AI revenue quality.
  • Broad company revenue, subscription growth, and cRPO are not directly attributable AI revenue.
  • Reported Data 360 / Headless / Other growth is not organic AI acceleration before the Informatica contribution is separated.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• If Agentforce and Data Cloud keep growing but the reported application buckets still do not show cleaner application-layer acceleration, the AI monetization case should be downgraded.
  • If Informatica comparability keeps obscuring organic quality, CRM has to move back to "product position is real, clean bridge is weak."
  • If customers treat AI as bundle enhancement rather than new budget, CRM becomes more of a defensive suite than an E9 core owner.

docs.text: Role: spine 9 endpoint / cloud / identity security Structural status: core Formal discovery state: Market-found Unified ledger: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: CrowdStrike makes money from endpoint, cloud, identity, SIEM, and incident-response subscriptions on the Falcon platform. Its spine-9 value is not owning the application or data itself, but providing billable security control when AI workloads, non-human identities, and cloud workloads move into production.

docs.title: 2026-08-26 Q2 FY2027 update
docs.text:
• Revenue was USD 1.47B, ARR USD 5.84B, net new ARR USD 332.8M, and Falcon Flex ending ARR exceeded USD 2.29B, up 101% year over year.
  • Operating cash flow and free cash flow were USD 530.3M and USD 377.4M. Management raised FY2027 net-new-ARR growth guidance to a 34% midpoint.
  • These are stronger Falcon-platform and Flex indicators, but the release does not separately disclose AI-security revenue, agent identity/security attach rates, module margin, or customer concentration; no official Q&A transcript was captured.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: CRWD primary-owns the endpoint / cloud / identity security control point in AI Application Production and Data Lifecycle, while remaining adjacent to distribution/platform surfaces in Platform Technology, Internet, and Distribution. It is not an application owner, data owner, E2 silicon owner, E6 systems owner, or E7/E8 physical-infrastructure beneficiary. Those monetization paths need their own pages and proof.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: When enterprises route agents, cloud workloads, identity planes, and endpoint fleets into Falcon, they can expand subscription scale through module attach, platform consolidation, and Falcon Flex. AI becomes revenue only through attach, module mix, and renewals. Total ARR, total revenue, or broader security spend are not automatically AI revenue.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• FY2026 ending ARR was USD 5.25B, up 24% year over year.
  • FY2026 Q4 net new ARR was USD 331M, up 47%, a record quarter.
  • Falcon Flex ending ARR was USD 1.69B, up 120%+.
  • The local 2026-06-28 SEC latest-route packet shows that subsequent locally visible filings were mainly Form 4 / 144 routes, with no newer operating print added to this page's source set.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• The prior FY2027 ARR guidance of USD 6.466B-6.516B is historical and superseded by the issuer outlook accompanying the Q2 update above.
  • Management describes Falcon as an AI security platform spanning GPU, agent, and prompt layers.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: If enterprise agents, identity sprawl, and cloud runtime keep expanding together, CrowdStrike can deepen platform attach across endpoint, identity, cloud, and SIEM.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• The company does not separately disclose AI revenue. Broad ARR and Falcon Flex ARR are not automatically AI ARR.
  • The "securing AI" narrative still needs finer attach-rate, module-penetration, and customer-outcome proof before it can be treated as a separate AI monetization line.

docs.title: Value capture and misread boundary
docs.text: CRWD captures value through platform consolidation, non-human-identity security, cloud-workload protection, and subscription expansion, not by becoming the application or data owner. The easiest misread is to treat any AI security budget as CrowdStrike revenue, or to blur endpoint / identity security into workflow, data-context permission, or recovery ownership.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• Platform attach slows, or Falcon Flex expansion stops converting into net new ARR.
  • Microsoft, PANW, or similar platform competitors compress cloud / identity / SIEM attach rates.
  • AI security language strengthens while the company still does not quantify more specific adoption, retention, or monetization outcomes.
  • Customer consolidation cycles lengthen, so growth comes more from price/bundle than real workload expansion.

docs.title: 2026-10-04 current conclusion
docs.text:
CRWD closed at USD270.04 on 2026-10-02. Equity value is 46.07x FY27 guide-midpoint revenue; Q2 FCF less SBC/payroll was negative USD22.001m. Revenue/ARR momentum is genuine, but cash economics do not support this valuation now. Group 3; large-position confirmation: NO.

docs.text: DDOG captures value through cross-cloud telemetry, AI workload observability, and security attach, not by owning application logic, enterprise data context, or physical compute. The easiest misread is to treat any GPU/LLM deployment as Datadog revenue, or to blur observability into workflow/control-plane ownership.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• Cloud optimization or workload efficiency compresses telemetry growth and product expansion.
  • Platform bundling, open-source/self-hosted tooling, or hyperscaler-native monitoring weakens attach rates.
  • AI workload monitoring remains feature adoption rather than a durable budget line.
  • Security and observability cross-sell stops reinforcing itself, so product count and cash conversion stop improving together.

docs.title: 2026-10-04 current conclusion
docs.text:
DDOG closed at USD277.22 on 2026-10-02. Equity/annualized Q2 revenue is 22.22x. After charging Q2 SBC, annualized FCF is only USD0.234996bn, or 423.58x equity/FCF-after-SBC. Group 3; large-position confirmation: NO.

For the current-add conclusion, see What Is Worth Buying. Action remains only with the unique SOT selected by Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger; a none row has no fallback, and this entity does not copy numeric zones or sizing.

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Dell designs, develops, manufactures, markets, sells, and supports infrastructure and client products. It reports through two segments: Infrastructure Solutions Group (ISG) and Client Solutions Group (CSG). The relevant piece here is ISG: AI-optimized servers, traditional servers and networking, storage, software, and deployment/support services.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: In spine 6, DELL is a branded systems and infrastructure delivery company. It is not a generic ODM/EMS, and it is not a single-component bottleneck owner. Its boundary is the packaged delivery of servers, networking, storage, and related services; upstream chip, optics, or component economics should not be assigned to DELL by default.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text:
• Q4 FY2026 disclosed more than USD 64B of full-year AI-optimized server orders, more than USD 25B of full-year shipments, and USD 43B of opening FY2027 backlog.
  • Q1 FY2027 disclosed USD 24.4B of AI orders booked and USD 16.1B of AI server revenue recognized; within that, AI-optimized servers revenue was USD 16.132B, up 757% year over year.
  • In the same quarter, ISG revenue was USD 29.009B, including USD 8.543B of traditional servers and networking revenue, up 92% year over year. That shows AI revenue is already recognized at the server layer while broader infrastructure content is also growing.
  • Q2 FY2027 disclosed USD 60.9B of AI orders, USD 16.4B of AI-server revenue, and USD 95B of ending AI backlog. ISG revenue was USD 31.8B, with USD 4.8B of operating income and a reported margin of about 15%.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• The 10-K states that DELL is organized around ISG and CSG; ISG addresses AI, machine learning, data analytics, and multicloud with integrated infrastructure solutions.
  • Q4 FY2026 disclosed >USD 64B of AI server orders, >USD 25B of AI server shipments for the year, and USD 43B of opening FY2027 backlog.
  • Q1 FY2027 disclosed USD 16.132B of AI-optimized server revenue, USD 29.009B of ISG revenue, USD 8.543B of traditional servers and networking revenue, and 10.5% ISG operating margin.
  • Q2 FY2027 disclosed USD 16.4B of AI-server revenue and USD 95B of ending AI backlog; ISG operating margin rose from 8.8% a year earlier to about 15%. Quarterly CFO was USD 2.225B, down 13%, and reported FCF was USD 0.986B, down 47%; the USD 8.149B adjusted FCF depended mainly on adding back financing receivables and leased equipment, so stronger profit proof does not remove the cash-conversion gate.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• In management commentary, Dell says enterprise and sovereign customers are increasing AI spending and that Dell AI Factories include networking, storage, and professional services.
  • The FY2027 AI-optimized server revenue guide increased from roughly USD 60B to USD 74B; it remains guidance, not a proven outcome.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• DELL monetizes AI through branded server and infrastructure system delivery and should no longer be framed only as a legacy PC company.
  • Traditional servers and networking also grew strongly in the same quarter as AI server scale-up, which likely means AI demand is pulling through broader system content. The exact attach mix is still not broken out.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• The revenue split for AI-driven storage, networking, and services.
  • Quarter-by-quarter stability of backlog conversion into revenue.
  • The sustainable margin profile of the AI systems business across changing customer and component mixes; AI-server margin is not separately disclosed.

docs.title: Operating and capital delta as of 2026-10-04
docs.text:
This section supersedes older “current/latest” framing. Reported results and management guidance not yet replaced by results remain period evidence and testable gates; an August issuance date alone does not make a still-future guide obsolete.

DELL’s AI-backlog/ISG evidence should be retained, but disclosed FCF fell 47% year over year and relies on receivable and lease add-backs; backlog cannot replace cash attributable to common owners. Recast old backlog/guide language as historical operating signal: revisit only if ISG margin and cash recover without those add-backs.

This round’s economic classification is Group 3 (not worth adding now). This page adds no price band, sizing, or execution trigger; What Is Worth Buying owns the four-group judgment and 大仓确认：NO remains in force.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• AI orders and backlog stop converting into recognized revenue for multiple quarters.
  • ISG margins deteriorate materially while AI mix rises, implying DELL is mainly a low-value pass-through.
  • Large customers shift AI-factory-level system integration to other system vendors or in-house designs, weakening DELL's delivery role.

docs.text: Core / Market-found branded systems/infrastructure anchor in spine 6. Q2 strengthened backlog-to-revenue, ISG-margin, and enterprise-customer-breadth proof together, but lower reported FCF, an adjusted-FCF bridge dominated by receivables/lease add-backs, and the absence of an AI-specific margin keep conversion durability open. docs.title: DOCN — DigitalOcean
docs.text: Role: spine 9 developer / inference runtime alternative cloud-compute benchmark Structural status: context Formal discovery state: Market-found Action route: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger selects Phase 3 AI Productionization Current-Live Deep Dive and TV Execution Zones as DOCN's sole current SOT; this entity carries no price bands, position sizing, or trade instruction.

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: DigitalOcean sells compute, storage, managed cloud, and AI infrastructure to developers, SMBs, and digital-native customers through subscriptions and usage. In spine 9, it is better treated as an alternative cloud-compute benchmark for smaller-scale AI app runtime, not as a hyperscaler, application/data owner, or physical-infrastructure owner.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: DOCN primary-owns the developer / inference runtime benchmark inside AI Application Production and Data Lifecycle, while remaining adjacent to smaller-scale cloud capacity in Cloud and Compute Demand. It is not a hyperscale demand anchor, does not primary-own the application/data layer, does not primary-own E2 silicon or E6 systems, and does not own E7/E8 physical infrastructure. This page keeps only the alternative-runtime mechanism and unit-economics boundary.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: Paperspace, GPU/AI compute, storage, and managed-service usage become recurring ARR and consumption revenue only when customers actually use that runtime. AI turns into revenue through inference/runtime usage, customer attach, and capacity utilization. Broad ARR, broad cloud revenue, or committed capacity are not automatically AI revenue.

docs.title: 2026-08-04 Q2 update
docs.text:
• Q2 2026 revenue was USD 281M, up 29% year over year; ARR was USD 1.125B, and AI Customer ARR was USD 234M, up 212%.
  • RPO was USD 894M, up about twelvefold year over year. Capacity obligations, conversion of RPO to revenue, and per-share free-cash-flow economics remain unresolved in the local evidence.

docs.title: 2026-08-07 SEC update: capacity financing and per-share economics
docs.text:
• RPO of USD 893.828M has a 3.7-year weighted-average term, with USD 365.901M / 40.9% expected in the next 12 months. Usage customers moving to commitments can raise RPO without equivalent incremental revenue.
  • GAAP gross margin fell from 59.9% to 55.0% as capacity costs preceded revenue. Adjusted FCF was USD 60.585M, up 6.3%, while its margin fell from 26.1% to 21.5%; the full-year margin guide was 11%-13%.
  • Finance-lease/equipment-financing liabilities rose from USD 130.514M at year-end to USD 577.720M; H1 added USD 414.902M of finance-lease right-of-use assets outside cash capex. Uncommenced colocation payments of USD 2.759B, server finance-lease payments of USD 281.566M and software commitments of USD 128.072M mean cash FCF is not the full capacity-economics measure.
  • GAAP diluted shares reached 126.548M, up 25.8%. July issuance of 12.544M shares raised about USD 1.474B gross before fees, with USD 471.828M used to retire 2030 converts. The roughly USD 1.003B arithmetic remainder is a post-quarter capital event, not June 30 cash or operating cash flow; it does not establish dilution-free deleveraging.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Q1 2026 revenue was USD 258M, up 22%; ARR was USD 1.032B, up 22%.
  • AI Customer ARR was USD 170M, up 221%; Million+ Dollar Customer ARR was USD 183M, up 179%.
  • RPO was USD 243M, versus USD 14M a year earlier.
  • Adjusted EBITDA was USD 105M / 41%.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• The 2026-07-07 preliminary update expected Q2 revenue growth of about 29%, RPO above USD 800M/more than 10x YoY, weighted contract duration above three years, and multiple nine-figure annual commitments. These were preliminary issuer claims at that date; the August 4 final Q2 results and August 7 SEC capture provide the subsequent evidence.
  • Total committed capacity is about 155MW; a new 20MW is expected in late 2027/early 2028.
  • The issuer says 81% of Q1 AI Customer ARR came from inference services and core cloud rather than bare-metal GPU rental. The definition still includes the customer's broader cloud revenue and is not pure AI-product ARR.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: Developer-first distribution and an integrated AI-native stack may win inference/agent workloads that do not require full hyperscaler complexity.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text: Q2 RPO of USD 893.828M is not automatically incremental revenue or take-or-pay. The next-12-month portion is disclosed as USD 365.901M / 40.9%; top-customer concentration, cancellation rights and capacity-level margin remain unresolved. 155MW is not full utilization or realized cash economics.

docs.title: Value capture and misread boundary
docs.text: DOCN captures value through developer-first runtime, price/performance, and a simpler AI app deployment surface, not through hyperscaler-scale demand ownership, application/data ownership, or physical buildout ownership. The easiest misread is to label all developer-cloud growth as AI runtime revenue, or to treat committed capacity as already realized cash economics.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• AI ARR, large-customer ARR, or RPO conversion decelerates repeatedly.
  • The 155MW capacity is delayed, underutilized, or requires excess financing; roughly USD 1.94B of Q1 disclosed/post-quarter facility obligations and the Q1 adjusted FCF margin of 1% are historical comparisons. The August 7 SEC update above lists the later Q2/post-quarter obligations; the older amount is not the current total.
  • Hyperscalers, neo-clouds, or inference platforms create price/performance pressure.
  • The disclosed July share issuance, note repurchase and hedge/capped-call treatment must be assessed together in the per-share bridge; dilution-free deleveraging wording cannot erase the shares actually issued.

docs.title: 2026-10-04 current conclusion
docs.text:
DOCN (DigitalOcean) closed at USD140.07 on 2026-10-02. USD16.470bn equity value is 14.02x FY26 guide-midpoint revenue, using the internally consistent 117.58m-share market basis. Growth is strong, but post-financing debt/share and cash conversion must be reconciled. Group 3; large-position confirmation: NO.

docs.title: EME — EMCOR Group
docs.text: Role: Phase 5 E8 spine 8 site electrical boundary to energized rack; EME is the MEP / EPC installation benchmark Structural status: context Formal discovery state: Market-found Evidence through: 2026-04-19; action SOT: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: EMCOR is not a platform selling electrical gear or cooling hardware. It is the construction and services organization that actually delivers the room's electrical, mechanical, fire, low-voltage, and operations stack. In E8 it benchmarks mission-critical MEP / EPC delivery capability rather than equipment ownership.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: EME covers the mission-critical installation and delivery layer after the site electrical boundary: electrical construction, mechanical construction, HVAC, plumbing, fire protection, low voltage, commissioning, facilities support, and operational readiness. It does not own upstream generation / fuel, and it does not own E6 servers / network systems. It sells build / install / maintain work, not generation assets, servers, or network equipment themselves.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: AI campus expansion eventually becomes real project execution. EME monetizes that through data-center design, core and shell work, prefabrication, electrical / mechanical installation, backup power, advanced cooling, commissioning, and Day 2 operations support. AI matters here because it raises mission-critical construction and services demand, not because EMCOR gets a hardware ASP.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• EMCOR's mission-critical page explicitly says it delivers end-to-end data-center solutions including infrastructure design and build, low-voltage installation, fire protection, and ongoing operations and maintenance.
  • The same page defines the full-lifecycle scope as initial design, core and shell construction, prefabrication, hardware installation, and ongoing maintenance and monitoring.
  • The electrical-construction section explicitly includes redundant back-up power systems, electrical distribution, and switchyards and switchgears.
  • The mechanical-construction section explicitly includes advanced cooling systems, HVAC, plumbing, fabrication, equipment installation, monitoring, and maintenance.
  • EMCOR also states it can provide 24/7/365 on-site mechanical and electrical systems support plus operational readiness and server / switchgear / router installation.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• EMCOR positions itself as a nationwide organization able to build, power, service, and protect data centers in highly regulated mission-critical environments.
  • Management language emphasizes full-lifecycle delivery and hyperscale mobilization capability, but the current raw packet does not directly attribute guidance or RPO to data centers as a standalone end market.
  • FY2025 Q4 results disclosed company-wide Remaining Performance Obligations of USD 13.25B, up 31.2% year over year, and 2026 revenue guidance of USD 17.75B–18.50B; those company-wide figures are not proof of AI or data-center revenue.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• If the AI buildout bottleneck is simply getting campuses built and kept operational, EMCOR-type MEP / EPC installers and service organizations are real beneficiaries.
  • Its economics are still construction-and-services economics, not the equipment-owner economics of cooling hardware, electrical gear, or server systems.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• The current raw packet does not provide data-center revenue share, mission-critical backlog / RPO split, or AI-project margin uplift.
  • There is also no evidence yet that EMCOR captures materially above-normal profit structure from AI data-center delivery versus ordinary large-project contracting.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• The mission-critical data-center capability is real, but if later filings still do not break out revenue / backlog / margin contribution, EMCOR should remain only a benchmark rather than move into higher-conviction status.
  • If hyperscale buildout slows or price competition compresses construction margins, EMCOR's AI read-through is more fragile than that of equipment platforms.
  • If critical scope shifts toward more vertical cooling, electrical, or modular specialists, EMCOR's bridge role in delivery weakens.

docs.text:
Classification: Group 2 — reopen only after the stated valuation and operating conditions; no current add.

Higher Q2 revenue, profit and RPO prove delivery capacity; RPO-to-revenue/margin/cash conversion, labor/claims and same-date valuation still need validation. Conditional watch.

docs.text:
Role: spine 5 manufacturing / packaging / test / materials active; materials / purity / contamination-control support layer Structural status: active Formal discovery state: Needs-source Evidence through: 2026-08-04

Action route: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger currently selects none for ENTG; there is no current action or fallback.

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Entegris mainly sells semiconductor materials plus filtration, purity, and contamination-control solutions. Its AI relevance comes from more complex advanced manufacturing and advanced packaging raising the need for purity, substrate integrity, and yield support, but it is not a direct packaging-equipment owner and the monetization bridge is still incomplete.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: ENTG primary-owns the materials / purity / contamination-control support layer inside Semiconductor Manufacturing, Advanced Packaging, Test, and Materials. It is not an OSAT, not an inspection / metrology tool, and not a direct compute platform; this page can only write it as a support layer for advanced manufacturing and advanced packaging.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: As device architectures, heterogeneous integration, and advanced packaging become more complex, customers need more purity, materials performance, substrate management, and yield support. ENTG's revenue bridge is currently proven only to the level of advanced manufacturing processes plus AI-related demand improving order patterns; it is not yet proven to a separate advanced-packaging / AI revenue split.

docs.title: 2026-08-04 Q2 update (historical disclosure; current framing is updated by the 2026-10-04 delta)
docs.text:
• Q2 2026 net sales were USD 883.2M, up 11.5% year over year; GAAP EPS was USD 0.61, non-GAAP EPS was USD 0.93, and adjusted operating margin was 24.5%.
  • Q3 guidance was sales of USD 905M-935M and non-GAAP EPS of about USD 1.01-1.09. The issuer did not provide a separate advanced-packaging, HBM, or AI-revenue split.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Q1 2026 net sales were $811.9M, up 5% YoY; non-GAAP diluted EPS was $0.86.
  • The same Q1 raw said revenue growth was primarily driven by unit-driven volumes related to the industry's most advanced manufacturing processes.
  • The Q4 2025 raw said 2025 unit-driven growth came from ongoing strength in liquid filtration, selective etch, and CMP consumables in the most advanced technologies.
  • Materials Solutions provides deposition materials, CMP slurries and pads, specialty gases, and etch / clean materials; Advanced Purity Solutions provides filtration, purification, and contamination control.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• Q1 2026 management said semiconductor demand continues to improve, AI-related demand is accelerating, and order patterns are strengthening; these are management attribution and trend claims.
  • Q4 2025 management said complex device architectures support AI growth and create higher content-per-wafer, purity, and yield-support opportunities; this remains forward opportunity framing.
  • The company positions its materials, filtration, and purification products as improving yield, device reliability, and purity, and says heterogeneous integration needs advanced materials, delivery, ESD, and substrate-management solutions.
  • Prior Q2 2026 guidance, given after Q1, was sales of $815M-$845M and non-GAAP EPS of $0.76-$0.84; Q2 actual results released on 2026-08-04 supersede that dated forecast.
  • Q4 2025 commentary about growth acceleration, higher content per wafer, and sustained market outperformance also remains issuer forward framing.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: ENTG is a real materials and yield-support layer for more complex AI-era manufacturing / advanced packaging, but its exposure is still indirect. The cleanest current write-up is “the support layer is real,” not “this is already a high-purity advanced-packaging monetization name.”

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• Advanced-packaging revenue, AI revenue, and HBM-related mix are not separately disclosed.
  • Named-customer or program-level advanced-packaging monetization proof is not disclosed.
  • It is not proven which exact product lines are driving the AI-related demand improvement.
  • It is not proven that ENTG deserves higher conviction than purer equipment, test, or inspection names.

docs.title: Operating and capital delta as of 2026-10-04
docs.text:
This section supersedes older “current/latest” framing. Reported results and management guidance not yet replaced by results remain period evidence and testable gates; an August issuance date alone does not make a still-future guide obsolete.

ENTG’s Q2 USD883.2m revenue and USD905–935m Q3 guide maintain a materials-platform recovery, but H1 AR/inventory use and about USD3.456bn debt net of unamortized discounts require CFO recovery and deleveraging together. The 7.96x FY2025-sales screen is not EV/revenue; do not let growth substitute for cash, debt, and working-capital validation.

This round’s economic classification is Group 2 (consider an addition only after the stated operating and valuation conditions close). This page adds no price band, sizing, or execution trigger; What Is Worth Buying owns the four-group judgment and 大仓确认：NO remains in force.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• The AI-related-demand and order-pattern-improvement language disappears without better segment evidence replacing it.
  • Advanced-packaging product positioning stays at the capability-showcase level instead of converting into verifiable content / yield economics.

docs.title: ETN — Eaton
docs.text: Role: Phase 5 E8 spine 8 site electrical boundary to energized rack; ETN is the broad electrical / UPS / switchgear benchmark Structural status: context Formal discovery state: Market-found Evidence through: 2026-05-05; action SOT: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Eaton is a large electrical platform spanning site-entry electrical, internal power distribution, power quality, modular power enclosures, and thermal adjacencies. It is not a single-theme data-center pure play. In E8 it is the benchmark used to calibrate broad electrical / UPS / switchgear exposure.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: ETN sits after the site electrical boundary and before the energized rack: power distribution, power quality, circuit protection, utility power distribution, services, cooling products, structural support systems, plus Fibrebond modular power enclosures. It does not own upstream generation / fuel, and it does not own E6 servers / network systems.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: When hyperscalers or colos expand capacity, AI-related spend first lands in site-entry electrical, distribution, power quality, and modular power enclosures. ETN's current monetization comes from selling its existing electrical platform and Fibrebond modular-power capability into data-center, utility, and industrial end markets.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• The FY2025 annual report and Q1 2026 10-Q define Eaton as an intelligent power management company serving data center, utility, industrial, commercial, and other end markets.
  • Management says Eaton is deepening participation across the electrical power value chain and benefiting from momentum in data-center and utility end markets.
  • Electrical Americas / Electrical Global products explicitly include power distribution and assemblies, power quality, circuit protection, utility power distribution, services, cooling products, and structural support systems.
  • Fibrebond is described as designing and building pre-integrated modular power enclosures for data-center and other customers.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• Eaton presents itself as a broad electrical platform serving multiple end markets rather than a narrow data-center subcategory.
  • The Boyd transaction language describes the target as a thermal-components and systems leader and says that, if completed, the deal would help serve hyperscale / colocation customers from chip to grid. That shows management wants critical liquid cooling inside the same electrical-platform story, but it is not proof of a completed portfolio expansion.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• Within E8, ETN is more useful as a benchmark than as a sharp mispricing call because it spans site power distribution, power quality, and modular power enclosures across the site-entry electrical bucket.
  • Its revenue base remains broad industrial and electrical exposure, so ETN should not be framed as a pure-play AI data-center winner.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• The current raw packet does not break out ETN's data-center revenue, UPS mix, or the standalone profit contribution of switchgear / cooling.
  • It is not yet proven that Fibrebond synergies or data-center exposure will durably change Eaton's growth profile across more reporting periods.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• Data-center and utility end-market momentum weakens enough to cool the AI read-through for the broad electrical platform.
  • Fibrebond modular power fails to show up in clearer order, revenue, or profit structure.
  • If ETN's data-center exposure remains only a broad-platform narrative without better attach-rate / mix evidence, the benchmark role should not be mistaken for a higher-conviction hidden thesis.

docs.title: FLNC — Fluence Energy
docs.text: Updated: 2026-09-09 CEST Industry page: Onsite Bridge Power, Storage, and Backup

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Fluence Energy's core business is battery energy storage systems, control software, and related services. It sells bridge storage, backup, and power-quality tools, not utility-generation asset ownership.

docs.title: 2026-08-05 Q3 FY2026 update
docs.text:
• Revenue was USD 649.848M, up 7.9% year over year, while GAAP/adjusted gross margin fell to 5.1%/5.9%. Net loss was USD 44.276M and adjusted EBITDA was negative USD 29.296M.
  • Q3 order intake exceeded USD 1.44B and contracted backlog was about USD 6.4B. The company reported about USD 850M of data-center business secured through July, including about USD 550M of July hyperscaler awards; these are award/order facts, not reported data-center revenue, margin, or cash-flow proof.
  • FY2026 revenue guidance fell to USD 2.9B-3.1B and adjusted-EBITDA guidance to negative USD 30M through positive USD 10M. Delivery, margin, and cash conversion remain the key evidence gaps.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text:
• It belongs to the Phase 5 E7 onsite / bridge storage segment inside the generation / grid / time-to-power causal lane.
  • The role boundary stops at storage, controls, and faster energization. It does not extend into site electrical distribution, rack power, cooling, or EPC spine 8.
  • Fluence's storage systems are not a utility-generation owner and are not a long-duration baseload owner.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: If AI data centers need faster interconnection, phased energization, backup, or power-quality support, Fluence can turn those needs into revenue through storage systems, control software, and project services. That path is a bridge / backup mechanism, not long-term generation ownership.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• The local product capture directly places Fluence storage solutions in the data-center use case.
  • The local issuer-primary case capture includes a Fluence / Centrica / Google Belgium backup-related example.
  • The local 10-Q and results captures are sufficient to establish that the company sells storage systems and software, not a generic theme proxy.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• The company presents storage for data-center use cases as faster deployment, interconnection support, backup, and power quality.
  • Company materials place storage in a bridge role for data-center power rather than in a primary baseload role.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• FLNC is best treated as Phase 5 E7 context because it helps define the boundary between storage exposure and onsite generation exposure.
  • It has a real lane use case, but it is closer to bridge storage than to onsite generation ownership.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• The page does not isolate AI-only revenue, AI-only backlog, or data-center-only storage revenue.
  • The page does not prove that data-center storage has become broad and repeatable enough to upgrade FLNC into a mainline core name.
  • The page also does not prove that storage here is the long-duration baseload role rather than the bridge / backup role.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• If future issuer-primary or filing evidence stops connecting Fluence storage systems to data-center bridge, backup, or interconnection use cases, this page's role should be downgraded.
  • If the current examples remain showcase-only and fail to produce repeat booking, deployment, or revenue evidence, the AI-to-revenue logic should be rewritten.
  • If the data-center narrative effectively collapses back into generic grid storage rather than the onsite / time-to-power lane, this page should leave Phase 5 E7 mainline tracking.

docs.title: FN Fabrinet
docs.text: Action route: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger selects MYCR, FN, and FORM AI Optical Manufacturing Current-Live Deep Dive and TV Execution Zones as FN's sole current SOT; this entity carries no price bands, position sizing, or trade instruction.

docs.title: Bottom line (historical disclosure; current framing is updated by the 2026-10-04 delta)
docs.text:
• Business: strong. FN is the difficult manufacturing-conversion layer for complex optics, DCI/transceivers, HPC, and communications systems. In Q4 FY2026, data center became the largest disclosed end market at USD 669M, up 68% year over year and equal to 51% of revenue.
  • Execution: strong. Q4 revenue was USD 1.316B, up 45%; FY2026 revenue was USD 4.641B, up 35.7%. Q1 FY2027 revenue guidance has a USD 1.400B midpoint, about 43% higher year over year and 6.4% higher sequentially.
  • Economics: not closed. Q4 non-GAAP gross margin was only 12.2%; Q4 FCF was USD -36.9M and FY2026 FCF only USD 4.2M. Growth is real, but working capital and the capacity build absorbed almost all cash generation.
  • Dated market and valuation observation. At 2026-08-18 05:11 ET, the USD 541 premarket indication was about 9.62% below the USD 598.58 prior regular close and implied roughly 31.4–32.9x third-party FY2027 EPS estimates. The early 540.02 / 544.00 bid/ask and thin volume did not establish regular-session liquidity.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text:
Within Systems, Racks, and Complex Manufacturing, FN owns complex optical/network manufacturing: process design, precision alignment, advanced optical packaging, integration, final assembly, test, and volume production.

It is not:

  • a branded network-system vendor with architecture control;
  • a generic server/rack ODM;
  • a pure play on optical chips, DSPs, lasers, or the full CPO architecture.

FN captures manufacturing, yield, engineering, and delivery value. It participates directly in AI/data-center optical demand, but its margin ceiling and customer bargaining position remain different from those of chip/IP and system platforms.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text:
The Q4 call's new end-market presentation makes the old datacom / telecom debate more actionable:

Q4 FY2026 end market Revenue YoY QoQ Share Data center USD 669M +68% +13% 51% Communications infrastructure USD 413M +40% +1% 31% Automotive, industrial and other USD 234M +8% +9% 18%

Attributed management commentary indicates that:

  • DCI was the largest contributor to data-center growth and had an annualized revenue run rate above USD 1B;
  • transceivers, DCI, and HPC are expected to keep driving Q1 FY2027;
  • new data-center transceiver programs may begin ramping in the current quarter, with a merchant program expected in the December quarter;
  • NPO is a nearer-term opportunity, while CPO work with several customers remains a future option rather than disclosed standalone revenue.

FN's AI exposure should therefore no longer be framed merely as “possibly part of broader datacom.” The remaining questions are program duration, customer quality, and whether capacity becomes margin and FCF.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• FY2026 revenue was USD 4.641B; GAAP EPS was USD 13.05; non-GAAP EPS was USD 14.09.
  • Q4 revenue of USD 1.3158B exceeded the prior USD 1.290B guidance high; non-GAAP EPS of USD 4.10 exceeded the prior USD 3.87 high.
  • Q1 FY2027 guidance is USD 1.375–1.425B of revenue and USD 4.10–4.25 of non-GAAP EPS.
  • Data center is now the largest Q4 end market; the growth can no longer be explained by a single legacy telecom/datacom label.
  • Cash plus short-term investments was about USD 875M, but both AR and inventory exceeded USD 1B, showing the rising capital intensity.

docs.title: Management claims / secondary call corroboration
docs.text:
• A DCI annualized run rate above USD 1B, new transceiver ramps, NPO/CPO customer work, and future USD 12.5–14B capacity are management outlook or secondary call-summary claims, not order commitments.
  • The call summary says four customers represented at least 10% of FY2026 revenue: Cisco 20%, Nvidia 16%, Nokia 11%, and Amazon 11%. Their combined 58% is more diversified than the older two-customer framing but is still high concentration.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• Committed program duration, pricing/yield, and project-level economics;
  • standalone NPO/CPO revenue, margin, and qualification timing;
  • utilization and return on invested capital for Building 10, Navanakorn, and Santa Clara;
  • whether FY2027 OCF/FCF catches up with revenue and EPS during the expansion cycle.

docs.title: Operating and capital delta as of 2026-10-04
docs.text:
This section supersedes older “current/latest” framing. Reported results and management guidance not yet replaced by results remain period evidence and testable gates; an August issuance date alone does not make a still-future guide obsolete.

FN has established recognized optical/DCI revenue, but FY2026 simple FCF was only about USD4.2m, customer agreements do not guarantee volume, and receivables/inventory plus concentration keep growth from automatically becoming capital returns. Recast old hold/trim or price language as historical; revisit only if growth becomes durable CFO under normal collections and incremental-capital returns.

This round’s economic classification is Group 3 (not worth adding now). This page adds no price band, sizing, or execution trigger; What Is Worth Buying owns the four-group judgment and 大仓确认：NO remains in force.

docs.title: Edge and economics
docs.text:
FN's moat is not a high-margin patent rent. It is difficult-to-replicate execution: complex optical processes, yield control, test, supply chain, customer qualification, and dependable NPI-to-volume production.

This can produce:

  • large revenue capture when multiple optical/network programs ramp;
  • customer reluctance to move difficult manufacturing flows;
  • operating leverage from a low opex ratio.

It does not automatically create a high gross margin. Q4 non-GAAP gross margin was 12.2% and operating margin 10.9%. Valuation must reflect concentration, working capital, and capex alongside the EPS beats.

docs.title: Capacity: growth asset and main risk (historical disclosure; current framing is updated by the 2026-10-04 delta)
docs.text:
• Building 10 is targeted for early-2027 completion, with about 2M sq ft; management estimated USD 3.0–3.5B of capacity depending on mix.
  • Pinehurst conversion, Navanakorn, and Santa Clara provide nearer-term space.
  • Management estimated current and planned additions could eventually support USD 12.5–14B of revenue capacity. That is potential capacity, not guidance.

The bull case is that visible customer ramps justify the build. The bear case is lower-than-planned utilization and structurally high working capital, turning revenue growth into weak FCF and ROIC.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• Data-center growth falls materially below guidance because of customer/program loss rather than shipment timing.
  • Aggregate concentration or pricing pressure from Cisco, Nvidia, Nokia, Amazon, or other large customers worsens.
  • Gross margin declines persistently and operating leverage cannot offset the damage.
  • FY2027 OCF/FCF still fails to catch revenue/EPS while inventory and AR grow faster than sales.
  • Building 10 or other capacity suffers delay, qualification failure, or poor utilization.
  • The market prices NPO/CPO as realized revenue before standalone shipment/economics proof exists.

docs.text:
Role: spine 5 manufacturing / packaging / test / materials active; FORM owns the probe-card / wafer-probe / test-interface exposure Structural status: active Formal discovery state: Market-found Evidence through: 2026-08-05

Action route: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger selects MYCR, FN, and FORM AI Optical Manufacturing Current-Live Deep Dive and TV Execution Zones as FORM's sole current SOT; this entity carries no price bands, position sizing, or trade instruction.

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: FormFactor mainly makes money from probe cards, wafer probe, and related test interfaces. Its AI relevance is not packaging outsourcing; it is the way HBM and more complex advanced packages raise the value of precision probing, thermal handling, and known-good-die discipline.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: FORM primary-owns the probe-card / wafer-probe / test-interface node inside Semiconductor Manufacturing, Advanced Packaging, Test, and Materials. It is not an HBM memory maker, not an OSAT, and not a CoWoS owner; TER — Teradyne is the broader ATE benchmark instead.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: As HBM stacks, TSV, thermo-compression bonding, and larger AI packages increase test complexity, memory makers need higher-value probe cards and tighter KGD discipline. FORM's clearest revenue bridge currently sits inside the DRAM bucket, where the issuer directly tied growth to demand for HBM designs used in generative AI applications.

docs.title: 2026-08-05 Q2 update (historical disclosure; current framing is updated by the 2026-10-04 delta)
docs.text:
• Q2 2026 revenue was USD 258.2M, up 31.9% year over year; GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins were 50.7% and 53.3%.
  • Q2 free cash flow was USD 52.6M. The local issuer pack still does not disclose absolute HBM revenue, customer concentration, or HBM-generation mix.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Q1 2026 revenue was USD 226.1M; Probe Cards revenue was USD 198.3M.
  • DRAM revenue was USD 82.93M, 36.7% of revenue, and up 69.7% YoY.
  • The issuer attributed DRAM growth primarily to increased demand for HBM designs used in generative AI applications, and the Q1 release also tied record DRAM revenue to HBM application demand.
  • The FY2025 10-K explicitly discussed DRAM including HBM and described packaging complexity tied to TSV and thermo-compression bonding.
  • The Q4 2024 release said FY2024 revenue growth was driven by HBM revenue growth and that HBM revenue increased fourfold versus the prior year.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text: • The current local raw packet does not provide a separate HBM revenue guide; any extension that HBM3E / HBM4 transitions will keep lifting FORM content should be treated as issuer framing until separately proven.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: FORM remains one of the cleanest U.S.-listed HBM probe-card / KGD candidates because the issuer tied revenue growth directly to HBM / generative-AI design demand rather than to a generic semiconductor recovery. Versus a broad ATE platform, its test-interface exposure is purer.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• Absolute HBM revenue is not separately disclosed, and the DRAM bucket still includes non-HBM demand.
  • Customer concentration and HBM3E / HBM4 mix are not disclosed.
  • It is not proven that the Q1 growth rate can cleanly persist through memory capex, qualification cycles, and generation transitions.

docs.title: Operating and capital delta as of 2026-10-04

docs.title: GEV — GE Vernova
docs.text:
Role: Phase 5 E7 spine 7 generation / grid / time-to-power; GEV owns the generation / grid equipment and service bridge Structural status: core Formal discovery state: Market-found Evidence through: 2026-08-19

Action route: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger selects GEV GE Vernova Current Live Deep Dive Conclusion as GEV's sole current SOT; this entity carries no price bands, position sizing, or trade instruction.

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: GE Vernova is not a power seller or merchant generator owner. It is an industrial platform selling generation equipment, grid equipment, and long-term services. Its core revenue comes from Gas Power, Electrification, and related service contracts, while Wind remains a separate business and volatility source.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: Within Power Generation, Grid, and Fuel Supply, GEV primary-owns the generation / grid equipment and service bridge. It covers gas turbines, utility-side transformers, utility-side switchgear, AC substations, HVDC, and service contracts that help power projects reach the grid faster. Ownership stops at the site / utility handoff; inside-the-fence switchgear, rack power, cooling, EPC, and server / network layers do not belong here.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: As data-center demand tightens power availability, utilities, developers, and power customers order gas turbines, transformers, utility-side switchgear, substations, HVDC, and long-term services to compress time-to-power. GEV therefore monetizes AI through equipment and service orders plus backlog, not through electricity sales.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Official Q1 2026 materials disclosed USD 18.3B of orders, +71% organic growth, and USD 13.0B of sequential backlog growth.
  • Gas Power equipment backlog increased from 40 GW to 44 GW, while slot reservation agreements increased from 43 GW to 56 GW.
  • Electrification equipment backlog reached USD 38.6B, up 75% year over year; the company booked USD 2.4B of equipment orders to support data centers in the quarter, more than all of last year.
  • Management attributed Electrification growth to switchgear / transformers in Power Transmission and AC substation / HVDC solutions in Grid Systems Integration.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• Management said demand is accelerating across both Power and Electrification and expects combined gas-turbine backlog plus slot reservations to reach at least 110 GW by year-end 2026.
  • The company describes the order momentum as coming from a diverse customer set, which implies data centers are a meaningful driver but not the only one.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• GEV is a bridge owner between generation buildout and grid connection, allowing it to capture early equipment and service spending when time-to-power becomes the bottleneck.
  • Revenue realization still depends on backlog conversion, delivery timing, and margin execution. Orders do not equal realized profit on day one.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• GEV's full Power / Electrification order book should not be treated as entirely AI-related, and current backlog should not be mechanically extrapolated into durable long-term margins.
  • The future share, delivery pace, and profit quality of data-center-related orders are not yet proven across a longer reporting history.

docs.title: 2026-08-19 Q2 10-Q follow-up
docs.text:
• Official Q2 FY2026 evidence is a positive proof break: orders were USD 24.2B (+88% organic), revenue USD 11.1B (+22% reported / +12% organic), adjusted EBITDA USD 1.2B, adjusted EBITDA margin 11.3%, and Q2 free cash flow USD 5.1B.
  • Backlog grew to USD 176B; Gas Power equipment backlog plus slot reservations rose from 100 GW to 116 GW, with management expecting at least 125 GW by year-end 2026. Electrification data-center orders reached more than USD 5B year to date.
  • FY2026 FCF guidance was USD 11.5B-12.5B.
  • The Q2 10-Q defines RPO as firm and unconditional customer orders and excludes purchase orders cancellable without a substantive penalty. But 1H operating cash flow of USD 10.680B included a USD 13.695B increase in contract liabilities/current deferred income, so FCF remains highly prepayment/working-capital sensitive. Wind, Prolec integration, and backlog conversion remain open evidence questions.
  • Official issuer transcript source gap: CLOSED. Q2 company-defined FCF was USD 5.107B, while the Q2 cash-flow bridge shows USD 8.121B of contract-liability/current-deferred-income inflow; the normalized-FCF gate remains PARTIAL and this cash-timing sensitivity cannot be annualized.
  • Wind Q2 segment EBITDA of $(275)M is a reported fact (CLOSED); Vineyard claims/counterclaims are BLOCKED-PUBLIC-DISCLOSURE. SRA-to-order/revenue, data-center mix/conversion, and Prolec integration/cash return remain PARTIAL; the earliest announced review is the 2026-10-28 Q3 official results/call.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• Gas Power backlog / slot reservations materially stall, cancel, or stop converting into deliverable projects.
  • Data-center-related Electrification orders slow materially, or backlog-to-revenue / margin performance degrades persistently.
  • Utility-side power projects are materially delayed or scope shifts down into inside-the-fence system integration, weakening GEV's generation / grid bridge ownership.

docs.title: 2026-10-04 frozen decision
docs.text:
Classification: Group 3 — not worth adding currently (not a sell call).

Q2 proves orders USD24.2bn, backlog USD176bn, revenue USD11.1bn, adjusted EBITDA USD1.2bn, FCF USD5.1bn and FY FCF guide USD11.5-12.5bn; however 1H operating cash flow included USD13.695bn contract-liability/current-deferred-income inflow and Wind Q2 EBITDA was negative USD275m. At 2026-10-02, GEV was USD988.70 at provider TTM/forward P/E 28.3x/47.3x. This is not a request for more AI orders: the same price does not compensate for working-capital-sensitive cash, Wind, Prolec and backlog-conversion risks. Move to group 3 not worth adding currently / large-position NO. Core/Market-found is no longer a current allocation judgment.
