docs.title: MYCR — Mycronic
docs.text:
Trading basis: Nasdaq Stockholm ordinary share; SEK; TradingView OMXSTO:MYCR Role: precision die bonding / photonic interconnect equipment; not an optical-module or CPO pure play Evidence through: 2026-08-05

Action route: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger selects MYCR, FN, and FORM AI Optical Manufacturing Current-Live Deep Dive and TV Execution Zones as MYCR's sole current SOT; this entity carries no price bands, position sizing, or trade instruction.

docs.title: Bottom line
docs.text: Mycronic is a high-margin precision-equipment group. Its MRSI die-bonding tools directly address the sub-micron placement, flip-chip, eutectic/epoxy bonding, and wafer-level processes that are difficult to automate in optical-module and silicon-photonics volume production. Vanguard Automation adds photonic wire bonding. Standalone revenue, customers, and profit for the optical businesses remain unquantified, so the correct framing is optics optionality inside the group, not a proven CPO pure play.

docs.title: Position in the chain and boundaries
docs.text:
• MRSI belongs to Global Technologies / Die Bonding, not PCB Assembly Solutions / former High Flex.
  • High Volume is a separate adjacency: AI-server thermal dispensing and optical-module dispensing/final assembly.
  • Vanguard / Photonic Interconnects can use 3D nano-printing to create low-loss optical connections at specific interfaces. It does not replace die attach, all fibre coupling, thermal/electrical interconnects, reliability, or testing.
  • MRSI-LEAP's <±1 µm at 3σ, >1,000 UPH, and 24/7 targets prove equipment capability, not customer qualification, sole-source status, yield, or CPO revenue.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text:
AI optics complexity → tighter die-placement / bonding tolerance → die-bonder demand → customer qualification / tool shipment → GT revenue and margin

The issuer has shown strong optical-communications demand for die bonders and new optical-module final-assembly opportunities in High Volume. What remains missing is a bridge from aggregate Global Technologies / High Volume data to MRSI optics, Vanguard, and CPO orders → shipments → revenue → margin.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• H1 2026 group orders were SEK 5,446M, up 61%; sales were SEK 4,919M, up 17%; EBIT margin was 33.2%.
  • Global Technologies H1 orders were SEK 2,026M, sales SEK 1,195M, and EBIT margin 30.9%; the issuer explicitly reported strong optical-communications demand for die bonders.
  • MRSI-LEAP explicitly covers AI optical modules, silicon photonics, flip-chip, UV epoxy, and wafer-level packaging.
  • Mycronic acquired Vanguard Automation on 2024-04-01; Vanguard's 2023 sales were EUR 5.2M.
  • A 2025 issuer feature still described Vanguard's customers as mainly research and innovation centres.

docs.title: Cannot be extrapolated
docs.text:
• All Global Technologies / High Volume revenue is not optics revenue.
  • The group's H1 33.2% margin cannot be assigned directly to MRSI economics; Pattern Generators contributed about 80% of H1 divisional EBIT.
  • Management explicitly described the customized SLX as a one-off, with delivery only in 2028; it cannot justify mechanically annualizing H1 EPS.
  • A product-scale photonic-wire-bonding claim is not volume-customer qualification.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• Standalone revenue, orders, backlog, customers, installed base, yield, ASP, or margin for MRSI optics, Vanguard, or CPO.
  • The scale at which Vanguard customers have moved from research/innovation centres to qualified volume manufacturers.
  • Whether High Volume optical-module final assembly produces recurring orders and sustainable margins.

docs.title: Financial and valuation facts
docs.text:
Net cash was SEK 2,267M on 2026-06-30. The normalized bridge uses about SEK 9,250M of sales, a trailing 23.85% EBIT margin, and roughly SEK 8.78 of normalized EPS; it does not simply double the favorable H1 Pattern Generators mix.

The 2026-08-04 regular-session price was SEK 324.40, about 36.9x normalized P/E, with a standard year-to-date return of +45.31%; these are dated market observations, not an instruction.

docs.title: Operating and capital delta as of 2026-10-04
docs.text:
This section supersedes older “current/latest” framing. Reported results and management guidance not yet replaced by results remain period evidence and testable gates; an August issuance date alone does not make a still-future guide obsolete.

MYCR’s H1 2026 sales were SEK4.919bn, EBIT SEK1.636bn, and operating cash SEK1.312bn, while its 2026 sales view rose to about SEK9.25bn; however, Pattern Generators still dominate profit and MRSI/Vanguard/optics have no standalone revenue or cash. An 8.81x FY2025-sales screen plus net cash supports only conditional observation, not conversion of aggregate orders into optics economics.

This round’s economic classification is Group 2 (consider an addition only after the stated operating and valuation conditions close). This page adds no price band, sizing, or execution trigger; What Is Worth Buying owns the four-group judgment and 大仓确认：NO remains in force.

docs.text:
• Global Technologies order growth comes mainly from non-optics businesses, while the optical sub-chain remains unquantified.
  • Vanguard remains concentrated in research/innovation-centre customers.
  • Pattern Generators mix/backlog normalizes and group earnings fall materially below the current bridge.
  • FX, working capital, or acquisition/intangible risks weaken cash conversion.
  • The share price advances faster than the evidence.

• Q2 revenue was USD 696.1M, up 36% year over year, and current RPO grew 35%.
  • GAAP operating loss was USD 205.7M, or 29.6% of revenue, while non-GAAP operating income was USD 96.1M, or 13.8% of revenue.
  • FY2026 revenue outlook was USD 2.864B-2.870B. AI/Workers paid-revenue attribution remains undisclosed, and no Q&A transcript was captured.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: NET primary-owns the edge / security / developer delivery surface in AI Application Production and Data Lifecycle, while remaining adjacent to developer distribution in Platform Technology, Internet, and Distribution. It is not an application/data owner, does not primary-own E2 silicon or E6 systems, and does not own E7/E8 physical infrastructure. The failure point it controls is edge delivery, API protection, and network security for AI apps and agent runtime.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: Revenue appears only when customers place AI apps, agents, APIs, and inference traffic on the edge runtime or network-security layer, driving Workers, delivery, security, and Zero Trust services. AI becomes revenue through usage, attach, and developer adoption. Broad network traffic, broad revenue, or total RPO do not automatically equal AI delivery revenue.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Q1 2026 revenue was USD 639.8M, up 34% year over year.
  • Current RPO growth was 34%.
  • Non-GAAP operating income was USD 73.1M; GAAP operating loss was USD 62.0M.
  • The local 2026-06-28 SEC latest-route packet shows that subsequent locally visible filings were mainly DEFA14A, Form 4, and 144 routes, with no newer operating print added to this page's source set.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text: • Management describes AI as a fundamental re-platforming of the Internet and one of the company's major tailwinds.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: If AI apps require lower-latency delivery, more API protection, more developer runtime, and tighter bot/agent security, Cloudflare's edge platform can expand attach and usage.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• The company does not separately disclose AI revenue. Broad revenue, RPO, or edge traffic are not automatically AI delivery monetization.
  • "AI is re-platforming the Internet" still needs more specific Workers / AI / security adoption and economics proof before it can be treated as a separate AI revenue line.

docs.title: Value capture and misread boundary
docs.text: NET captures value through edge delivery, developer surface, and security attach, not by becoming an alternative hyperscaler, server owner, or facility-infrastructure beneficiary. The easiest misread is to write all AI network traffic as Cloudflare revenue, or to blur the developer edge platform into application/data ownership.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• AI-related usage stays mostly narrative, without clearer attach, retention, or revenue proof.
  • Hyperscaler, CDN, SASE, and developer-platform competition compress pricing or attach rates.
  • Developer/runtime adoption expands while GAAP losses and unit economics do not improve.
  • Edge/security demand grows without translating into a higher-quality recurring-revenue mix.

docs.title: 2026-10-04 current conclusion
docs.text:
NET closed at USD349.07 on 2026-10-02. Equity/annualized Q2 revenue is 44.62x. Q2 FCF less disclosed SBC/payroll proxy is negative USD84.193m and GAAP operating loss was USD205.7m. Group 3; large-position confirmation: NO.

For the current-add conclusion, see What Is Worth Buying. Action remains only with the unique SOT selected by Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger; a none row has no fallback, and this entity does not copy numeric zones or sizing.

docs.text: Role: spine 4 IP / optical connectivity context Structural status: context Formal discovery state: Needs-source Evidence through: 2026-06-05; action SOT: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Nokia earns from platform-scale network businesses across Network Infrastructure, Mobile Networks, and Cloud and Network Services. Its AI relevance mainly comes through optical, IP, data-center networking, and the Infinera addition, but this page remains context because the company-level AI / cloud story is not yet split into stable enough product-level revenue proof.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: Nokia primary-owns the IP / optical connectivity large-platform node in AI Interconnect, Optical Networking, and DCI. It is not a pure switch vendor, pure optical-module vendor, or single data-center silicon name; mobile, fixed, and broader telecom mix still dilute the primary lane.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: When AI / cloud customers buy optical line systems, pluggables, IP routing, data-center switching, and intra-data-center optics, the revenue should first appear inside Network Infrastructure, Optical Networks, and IP Networks. To write this as a stronger thesis, the page still needs more stable product-level or customer-level revenue bridges.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• In Q1 FY2026, AI & Cloud customer net sales grew 49% and were 8% of group sales.
  • Nokia booked EUR 1B of AI & Cloud customer orders in the quarter.
  • In the same quarter, Network Infrastructure net sales grew 6%, including 20% growth in Optical Networks.
  • The official data-center networking page explicitly places high-performance switches, optics, and IP / optical interconnect inside data centers and to / from / between data centers, including 800GE and intra-data-center optics.
  • Nokia says the Infinera deal expands webscale exposure; official materials state that webscale / ICP customers were over 30% of Infinera sales and that Infinera had been developing high-speed, low-power intra-data-center optical components suited to AI workloads.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• Management raised the 2026 Network Infrastructure growth assumption to 12%-14% and the Optical + IP Networks growth assumption to 18%-20%.
  • Nokia raised its 2025-2028 AI & Cloud addressable-market CAGR assumption to 27%.
  • New DSP / optical solution timing from OFC remains product and volume-roadmap language that still needs follow-through.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: Nokia has real AI / cloud optical and IP exposure, but it still looks more like one growth pocket inside a large platform than a standalone pure AI interconnect asset.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• A durable revenue split from AI / cloud into optical, IP, switching, or Infinera content is not proven.
  • It is not proven that AI / cloud orders are already converting into a structurally better profit mix.
  • It is not proven that the AI optical / IP story can outweigh legacy mobile / fixed / telecom cycle noise.

docs.title: Operating and capital delta as of 2026-10-04
docs.text:
This section supersedes older “current/latest” framing. Reported results and management guidance not yet replaced by results remain period evidence and testable gates; an August issuance date alone does not make a still-future guide obsolete.

NOK’s Q2 AI & Cloud sales/orders prove its DCI/platform role, but legacy mix, restructuring, and integration still decide cash. On the explicit 1 ADS = 1 ordinary-share and EURUSD 1.1225 basis, the 2.73x FY2025-sales screen is relatively low but not an automatic buy; AI/Cloud orders must become margin and cash, and the old starter band is no longer current.

This round’s economic classification is Group 2 (consider an addition only after the stated operating and valuation conditions close). This page adds no price band, sizing, or execution trigger; What Is Worth Buying owns the four-group judgment and 大仓确认：NO remains in force.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• AI & Cloud orders fail to keep converting into revenue or margin.
  • Optical / IP growth gets offset by weakness in other large segments.
  • Infinera integration, R&D burden, or execution complexity erodes returns.
  • Data-center networking products fail to win durable share and the AI exposure falls back to concept-level relevance.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: NOK is a Context / Needs-source large-platform IP / optical connectivity reference name. It helps explain the mainline, but current proof is still too broad to support a stronger pure AI interconnect conclusion.

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: ServiceNow turns deployed compute into enterprise workflow and system-of-action platform revenue. The real test is not the model itself but whether AI moves from answering questions into governed workflow execution and then into durable ACV, subscription, and RPO growth.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text:
• Lane: E9 AI Application Production and Data Lifecycle workflow / platform AI owner, centered on ITSM, CSM, HR, and enterprise-operations governed execution.
  • Boundary: it owns workflow, approval, ticket, and orchestration layers. It does not own E2 compute silicon, E6 systems manufacturing/integration, or any E7/E8 power and facility layer.
  • Distinction: NOW owns the workflow-execution control point. It is not CRM's customer-data control plane and not hyperscale cloud infrastructure.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text:
• The core platform subscription base still carries the main seat and workflow revenue.
  • Now Assist, Context Engine, Autonomous Workforce, and Build Agent Skills can expand contract value if they increase attach and net-new ACV.
  • cRPO and RPO show future contract conversion, but broad subscription growth, cRPO, and total revenue are not direct AI revenue.

docs.title: Proven — Q2 current baseline; Q1 retained for historical comparison
docs.text:
• Q2 subscription revenue was USD 3.877B, up 24.5% reported / 23% constant currency; total revenue was USD 3.987B, up 24% / 22.5% constant currency.

  • Q2 cRPO was USD 13.20B, up 21% reported / 21.5% constant currency; RPO was USD 29.0B, up 21% / 22% constant currency. AI ACV crossed USD 1B; ACV is not recognized AI revenue.

  • Q1 FY2026 subscription revenue was USD 3.671B, up 22%.

  • Q1 FY2026 total revenue was USD 3.770B, up 22%.
  • cRPO was USD 12.64B, up 22.5%.
  • Total RPO was USD 27.7B, up 25%.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• The count of Now Assist customers spending more than USD 1M in annual contract value grew more than 130% year over year.
  • There were 16 net-new ACV transactions above USD 5M, nearly +80% year over year.
  • Context Engine, Autonomous Workforce, Build Agent Skills, and EmployeeWorks were all named directly in the Q1 issuer packet.
  • Q2 disclosed 123 net-new-ACV transactions above USD 1M, 658 customers above USD 5M ACV and 9x growth in agentic deployments over nine months. These are distinct from the Q1 counts above.
  • FY2026 subscription-revenue guidance includes about 125 bps of Armis contribution and management-expected operating-margin and FCF-margin headwinds. This is forward comparability framing, not a realized result.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• NOW sits at the workflow-execution and governance node, so it has one of the cleanest paths to turn enterprise AI from assistant behavior into governed action.
  • If more cross-system workflows consolidate on NOW, AI can expand platform spend rather than just add a feature to existing seats.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• The USD 1B AI ACV disclosure closes the older customer-count-only gap; it is not a recognized AI revenue, gross-margin or organic-versus-acquired revenue waterfall.
  • Broad subscription revenue, cRPO, and RPO are not directly attributable AI revenue.
  • Current disclosure does not fully separate organic workflow/AI growth from the Armis contribution.

docs.title: Cash, acquisitions and current boundary — 2026-10-04
docs.text:
At the September investor conference, management described realized 20%-30% new-AI-package uplifts, about 30% Prime uplift and over 50 customers paying at least USD 1M annually for new AI packages. This strengthens paid-contract evidence without isolating renewal, incremental revenue or contribution margins.

H1 OCF, cash capex and SBC were USD 2.257B, USD 0.255B and USD 1.213B; business-combination cash was USD 8.776B and repurchases USD 2.225B. Acquisition growth, financing and shareholder distributions are not one FCF measure. The 10-Q says acquired results were not material individually or in aggregate: it does not support calling Q2 primarily acquisition-led, nor an invented exact organic split.

The 38m plan-share S-8 and assumed AI.Work / Sweep awards are future capacity, not issued dilution. Test core renewal, contract profit, post-acquisition cash and net shares; missing standalone AI revenue does not substitute for whole-business analysis.

The old July USD 95.46 starter and reset lines have no current execution meaning. Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger selects only Enterprise Software Platform Current-Live Two-Batch Writeback Ledger as NOW's action owner. This entity has no numeric bands; large-position confirmation: NO.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• If Now Assist and Autonomous Workforce improve product narrative but fail to expand net-new ACV, NOW should fall back to a feature-strength story.
  • If workflow AI stays in pilot mode rather than governed production execution, the E9 owner case weakens.
  • If Armis contribution or integration headwinds keep obscuring organic net-new ACV and cash quality, NOW's benchmark quality should be downgraded.

docs.title: NVDA — NVIDIA
docs.text: Role: spine 2 accelerator platform / system architecture Structural status: core Formal discovery state: Market-found Evidence through: 2026-08-26

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: NVIDIA earns from GPUs/accelerators, networking, systems, and enterprise software licenses/subscriptions. Its moat is the combined CUDA, interconnect, system design, and release cadence—not one GPU. AI workloads first become compute/networking shipments; mix, pricing, and software attach determine profit and cash.

docs.title: 2026-08-26 Q2 FY2027 update (historical disclosure; current framing is updated by the 2026-10-04 delta)
docs.text:
• Revenue was USD 96.221B and Data Center revenue USD 89.0B, up 117% year over year. Q3 revenue guidance was USD 108B +/-2% without assuming China Data Center compute revenue.
  • Supply and capacity commitments were USD 279B, total future commitments USD 366B, total maximum guarantee exposure USD 108.5B, accounts receivable USD 63.1B with DSO of 60 days, inventory USD 31.6B, and Q2 senior-note issuance USD 25.0B.
  • The release advances demand and platform-execution proof while expanding the capital-intensity, customer-financing, receivable, inventory, and guarantee evidence to monitor.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: NVDA primary-owns the accelerator platform in Semiconductors and Foundational Compute. HBM belongs to Memory, Storage, and In-System Data Movement, wafer/package realization to Semiconductor Manufacturing, Advanced Packaging, Test, and Materials, and rack manufacturing to Systems, Racks, and Complex Manufacturing. These dependencies do not belong inside NVIDIA's primary lane.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: Cloud, enterprise, and sovereign customers buy GPU, NVLink/NVSwitch, networking, and systems. Platform value comes from system ASP, software/services, iteration speed, and switching cost. Returns still depend on supply, gross margin, cash conversion, and installed-base utilization.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Q1 FY2027 revenue was USD 81.6B, up 85%; Data Center revenue was USD 75.2B, up 92%.
  • Data Center compute revenue was USD 60.4B, up 77%; networking revenue was USD 14.8B, up 199%.
  • GAAP/non-GAAP gross margin was about 74.9%/75.0%, showing strong current value capture.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text: NVIDIA attributes future growth to agentic/physical AI, AI factories, and expansion beyond hyperscale. This forward claim needs later revenue-mix proof.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: Software, interconnect, and systems integration raise switching costs and let NVIDIA capture more than single-chip value.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text: Current growth and margin cannot be perpetually extrapolated. Not all hyperscaler capex becomes NVIDIA revenue, and custom silicon, export controls, or supply shifts can change share and pricing.

docs.title: Operating and capital delta as of 2026-10-04
docs.text:
This section supersedes older “current/latest” framing. Reported results and management guidance not yet replaced by results remain period evidence and testable gates; an August issuance date alone does not make a still-future guide obsolete.

NVDA’s revenue and cash performance are strong, but cloud agreements, third-party leases, and guarantees cannot be merged into either zero risk or all debt. The 26.11x screen on FY2026 USD215.938bn sales predates the latest quarter; the USD108bn ±USD2bn Q3/74% GM guide must be tested with receivables, inventory, and capital commitments rather than deployment scale alone.

This round’s economic classification is Group 2 (consider an addition only after the stated operating and valuation conditions close). This page adds no price band, sizing, or execution trigger; What Is Worth Buying owns the four-group judgment and 大仓确认：NO remains in force.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• Data Center growth, gross margin, or networking attach slows materially for several periods.
  • Large customers increase custom silicon and weaken accelerator share or bargaining power.
  • Export limits, advanced packaging/HBM supply, or system delivery blocks recognized revenue.
  • Competing platforms close the software/system total-cost gap.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text:
NVDA is the Core / Market-found compute-platform anchor. The market already recognizes its AI role.

Current action is routed only by Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger; NVDA is currently none, with no fallback.

docs.title: Business and primary lane
docs.text: Novo Nordisk earns from diabetes and obesity medicines. GLP-1 demand must translate through realized pricing, reimbursement and competition into durable profit. Primary lane: Pharma and Biotechnology.

docs.title: Current operating evidence

Proven: Q2 2026 adjusted sales were DKK78.488B (+7% CER) and adjusted operating profit DKK33.389B (+11%). The definitions exclude US 340B provision reversals and, for profit, DKK6.3B of non-cash pipeline impairment including monlunabant DKK4.0B.

Inference: the GLP-1 franchise has economic value; the old unrefreshed claim that valuation was inexpensive cannot establish a current add.

docs.title: Risks and falsifiers
docs.text: Obesity competition, realized prices and reimbursement jointly determine growth. Volume that cannot offset pricing pressure, or further pipeline losses, can make a low headline multiple misleading. One-off 340B effects are not normalized growth.

docs.title: NVT — nVent
docs.text: Role: Phase 5 E8 spine 8 site electrical boundary to energized rack; NVT is the enclosures / connectivity / liquid-cooling / power-distribution benchmark Structural status: context Formal discovery state: Market-found Evidence through: 2026-05-01; action SOT: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: nVent sits closer than ETN to the rack-adjacent mix of enclosures, power connections, control buildings, and cooling. It is not a generation owner or a server owner. In E8 it is the benchmark for rack-entry electrical / cooling exposure.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: NVT covers the inside-the-fence electrical and room-entry layer: cable management, control buildings, liquid / air cooling, electrical connections, enclosures, equipment protection, power connections, bus systems, switchgear systems, and power distribution solutions. It does not own upstream generation / fuel, and it does not own E6 servers / network systems.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: As AI data-center density rises, rack-adjacent demand also rises for enclosures, power connections, busway, control buildings, PDU support, liquid-cooling support, and mission-critical protection. NVT monetizes AI by helping deliver power and thermal management safely to the rack rather than by selling compute.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• The annual report and Q1 2026 10-Q state that nVent's portfolio includes cable management, control buildings, liquid / air cooling, electrical connections, enclosures, equipment protection, power connections, and power management solutions.
  • Systems Protection is defined as serving mission-critical applications including data centers and includes custom enclosures, liquid / air cooling, control buildings, switchgear systems, and power distribution solutions.
  • The Electrical Products Group acquisition is described as infrastructure solutions primarily for power utilities and data centers, operated mainly within Systems Protection.
  • The SC25 issuer product capture shows nVent actively selling a liquid-cooling and power portfolio into data-center and networking infrastructure.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• nVent describes itself as an enclosures and liquid-cooling leader and explicitly targets data-center / networking infrastructure as an application lane.
  • Company-wide backlog increased from USD 749.3M at year-end 2024 to USD 2.3499B at year-end 2025; management attributed the increase mainly to the Electrical Products Group acquisition and growth in the data-centers business and expected most backlog to ship in 2026. That company-wide total is not AI-backlog proof.
  • Q1 2026 disclosed USD 75.8M of acquired customer backlog with an estimated useful life of about three years, showing management tracks acquired backlog conversion, but that still does not equal fully closed organic AI monetization.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• Within E8, NVT is a more focused benchmark than ETN for rack-entry electrical / cooling because it directly covers the enclosure, connection, power-distribution, and liquid-cooling stack.
  • Backlog growth still reflects both acquisition and data-center growth, so the stronger evidence should not be translated mechanically into all-organic AI upside.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• The current raw packet still does not provide clean hyperscaler / data-center revenue share, organic backlog-growth split, or standalone margin disclosure for liquid cooling / power distribution.
  • former-half-hidden remains only a workflow modifier and should not be treated as a formal state or as a hidden-thesis conclusion.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• If backlog growth remains mostly acquisition-driven without clearer organic data-center conversion, NVT's AI beneficiary profile is being overstated.
  • If the enclosure / connectivity / liquid-cooling offering does not translate into clearer customer, revenue, or margin proof, the benchmark role should remain context-only.
  • If data-center spend cools and NVT cannot prove durable attach rates for rack-entry electrical / cooling, the current positioning should not be upgraded.

docs.title: 2026-10-04 frozen decision
docs.text:
Classification: Group 2 — reopen only after the stated valuation and operating conditions; no current add.

Retain Q2 operating update and product leads; adding requires order/backlog-to-margin/cash conversion, acquisition integration and same-date valuation. The registry is none; conditional watch.

  • Action boundary: the unified registry is currently none, with no fallback and no numeric zone, sizing, or TradingView authority.

docs.title: Lane and boundary

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue

docs.title: Proven

docs.title: Reasonable inference

docs.title: Not proven

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Oklo is an advanced-fission project developer focused on future power delivery. In this wiki it represents whether future microreactors and advanced nuclear projects can turn into faster data-center power, not present-day facility infrastructure or onsite electrical equipment.

docs.title: Lane and boundary

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text:
• Realized results: the local raw packet proves that the company has disclosed data-center/campus strategic relationships, power-availability partnerships, and business updates.
  • Forward path: the AI/data-center narrative reaches realization only if those relationships turn into executed contracts, verifiable project progress, regulatory advancement, and realized revenue.
  • Current conclusion: the local evidence proves forward contract/cooperation direction, not realized data-center revenue or stable operating output.

docs.title: 2026-08-07 Q2 official update
docs.text:
• Groves achieved first criticality on 2026-08-05. The issuer also reported Aurora-INL DOE PDSA approval with site development/construction advancing, an Ohio/Kiewit planning MOU, and Meta demand visibility for phased Aurora deployment.
  • Q2 revenue was USD 1.210M, Q2 net loss was USD 48.536M, six-month net loss USD 81.601M, and six-month operating cash flow negative USD 65.459M; the reported revenue was not commercial power revenue.
  • Cash plus marketable securities were USD 3.006B at 2026-06-30, including about USD 1.9B from first-half ATM offerings. This improves runway but does not close project economics.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:

  • Issuer / power-availability partnership: material on accelerating power availability

  • Conclusion: this is a positive partial future-generation benchmark; the local packet now includes deployment-process, regulatory, demand-visibility, and financing evidence but not commercial power revenue or margin proof.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text: Company materials emphasize its advanced-nuclear platform, long-term power relationships, and positioning around faster data-center power availability.

docs.title: Reasonable inference

docs.title: Current role

  • Boundary: owns the inspection and metrology role in HBM / 2.5D / advanced packaging; does not treat ONTO as a generic semiconductor-equipment proxy

docs.title: 2026-08-06 Q2 earnings update (historical disclosure; current framing is updated by the 2026-10-04 delta)
docs.text:
• Q2 revenue was USD 343.1M, up 35.3% year over year and nearly 18% sequentially.
  • Advanced Nodes revenue grew 50% sequentially to a record, while Specialty Devices and Advanced Packaging reached an all-time high, supported by 2.5D logic, HBM, and silicon-photonics demand.
  • Backlog exceeded USD 1B for the first time. The company-wide AI revenue ratio, customer/order concentration, and valuation remain unclosed.

docs.title: Business and lane position
docs.text: Onto defines itself in the issuer raw as a process-control leader spanning 3D metrology, macro defect inspection, factory analytics, and advanced semiconductor packaging. For spine 5, its key ownership is not broad semiconductor capex but the process-control / metrology node inside HBM, fan-out, and 2.5D advanced packaging.

docs.title: AI to revenue
docs.text: The AI transmission has reached order / VPA and qualification evidence. In fiscal 2025, revenue was $1.0053 billion, and the company disclosed a new Dragonfly volume purchase agreement worth more than $240 million with a leading HBM manufacturer for 2D inspection and 3D bump metrology supporting expansion through 2027. It later disclosed Dragonfly G5 qualification for 2.5D AI packaging. The cleaner framing is that AI / HBM / advanced packaging have entered product orders and platform validation, while the local raw still does not provide a company-wide AI revenue ratio.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Fiscal 2025 revenue reached $1.0053 billion, and fourth-quarter revenue was $267 million.
  • The company disclosed a new volume purchase agreement worth more than $240 million with a leading HBM manufacturer for Dragonfly 2D inspection and 3D bump metrology supporting expansion through 2027.
  • Dragonfly G5 was qualified for 2.5D AI packaging.
  • The company defines itself as an advanced-packaging-related process-control supplier spanning wafer and package inspection / metrology.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• Management said global AI investment is driving a strong upcycle in semiconductor capital-equipment spending.
  • Initial Dragonfly G5 shipments are expected to begin in June 2026, and Dragonfly platform revenue is expected to grow more than 50% in 2026 versus 2025.
  • The early first-quarter preliminary revenue and second-quarter guidance are dated preliminary disclosures; the August 6 Q2 actual revenue of USD 343.1M supersedes that prior Q2 forecast.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: • Rising HBM, chiplet, fan-out, and 2.5D / 3D packaging complexity should increase package-level inspection and metrology content and sensitivity requirements.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• Company-wide AI revenue share.
  • AI demand is already strong enough to create durable margin expansion; 2025 operating margin was still below the prior year.

docs.title: Operating and capital delta as of 2026-10-04
docs.text:
This section supersedes older “current/latest” framing. Reported results and management guidance not yet replaced by results remain period evidence and testable gates; an August issuance date alone does not make a still-future guide obsolete.

ONTO’s Q2 USD343.129m revenue, 53.4% gross margin, and above-USD1bn backlog prove metrology demand, but backlog lacks a mix/conversion schedule and 0% notes/investment items cannot be netted from equity/sales.   • Dragonfly demand stops broadening across customers and process layers.
  • The advanced-packaging process-control story gets fully overwhelmed by a broader wafer-equipment cycle.

docs.title: ORCL — Oracle
docs.text:
Role: spine 1 demand / capacity economics Structural status: core Formal discovery state: Market-found Evidence through: 2026-10-04; latest completed market session: 2026-10-02

Current-evidence filter: the September 10 FY27 Q1 release and 10-Q control operating judgment, supplemented by the October 2 Point Beach announcement. The September 16 Futu quote and FY26 Q4/10-K are dated historical comparisons, not current valuation or buy evidence.

docs.title: October 4: operating growth has not removed common-equity funding burdens
docs.text:
Q1 operating cash flow includes USD 11.363B of financing-component customer prepayments and a separate USD 3.997B increase in other deferred revenue. Neither is current revenue or automatically recurring cash generation. Net ATM proceeds of USD 19.909B correspond to about 141M issued common shares: funding and dilution, not profit realization.

Uncommenced leases total USD 288B, generally starting from FY27 Q2 through FY29 for 15–19 years, alongside separately disclosed USD 34.150B supply/power obligations. These categories are not mechanically additive current book debt. The October 2 Point Beach plan involves approximately USD 300M of energy costs, subject to regulatory approval; it is not cash already paid or automatically incremental to existing obligations.

The October 2 regular close was USD 142.30. Provider equity value of USD 431.38B divided by provider TTM sales of USD 71.78B is about 6.01x equity/sales, not EV/sales. Negative FCF, advance funding, issued shares and long-term capital obligations support not adding currently; registry none is not the economic reason. Reassessment requires OCI delivery growth to improve financed per-share cash, not merely RPO. The four-group overview is What Is Worth Buying, while action remains routed solely through the unified ledger.

docs.title: 2026-09-16 Q1 evidence refresh — conversion is visible, financing still matters
docs.text:
• Q1 FY2027 cloud revenue was USD 11.607B, up 62%, and OCI/IaaS was about USD 7.4B, up 121%. Oracle says it delivered another 850MW of data-center capacity and more than 300,000 GPUs, advancing the RPO-to-capacity-and-revenue chain from forecast to partial delivery.
  • RPO rose to USD 664B, with more than USD 30B of new AI-cloud contracts signed in Q1. RPO remains neither cash, current revenue, utilization, nor a high-margin guarantee.
  • GAAP OCF was USD 23.103B, including a USD 11.363B deferred-revenue increase from customer prepayments with a significant financing component. Gross capex was USD 28.499B, and company-defined FCF was USD -5.396B. Conversion has not removed capital intensity.
  • The ATM equity program generated USD 19.909B of net cash. Oracle's supplemental USD 17.966B net-cash-outlay-for-capex measure subtracts customer prepayments and specified financing cash flow; it cannot replace GAAP FCF or double-count the benefit.
  • The 850MW disclosure does not identify IT load versus campus capacity, utilization, location, network architecture, or suppliers. It cannot be attributed to AVGO, NVDA, VRT, GEV, or another single name.

docs.title: 2026-08-20 FY2026 historical baseline — not current valuation
docs.text:
• FY2026 Q4 RPO reached USD 638B, up USD 85B sequentially; Q4 OCI/IaaS revenue was USD 5.787B (+93% year over year), while FY2026 OCI/IaaS revenue was USD 18.101B (+77%).
  • The same FY2026 evidence records USD 55.663B capex, USD 31.977B operating cash flow, and USD -23.686B FCF, alongside USD 129.541B borrowings, USD 31.894B cash/securities, major lease commitments, and future financing plans. Demand strength therefore does not close the capital, delivery, margin, or per-share conversion question.
  • RPO is staged contracted revenue, not an energized-capacity, utilization, supplier-allocation, or margin guarantee. About USD 75B of large-AI-contract RPO reflects customer-prepaid or customer-supplied GPU hardware and must not be relabeled as Oracle-funded supplier demand.
  • The August price and valuation snapshots remain in raw history only; they are excluded from current valuation and action.

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Oracle earns subscription and usage revenue from databases, enterprise applications, and OCI. Its AI-chain role is not making chips, power, or facility equipment; it converts long-duration cloud contracts into capacity that must be delivered. The central test is whether RPO becomes capacity, revenue, margin, and cash on schedule.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: Oracle is a demand anchor in Cloud and Compute Demand. It buys GPU, network, storage, land, power, and facility delivery for enterprise and AI customers. Unlike suppliers such as NVDA, VRT, or BE, Oracle operates the capacity; its capex alone does not prove any supplier's revenue attribution.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: OCI, database, and application contracts first enter RPO. Revenue is recognized as Oracle delivers capacity and services. AI raises compute usage and campus intensity, but value capture depends on delivery speed, contract mix, pricing, financing cost, and post-capex cash conversion.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Q1 FY2027 cloud/OCI revenue was USD 11.607B/about 7.4B, up 62%/121%, and Oracle says it delivered 850MW of additional data-center capacity.
  • Q1 OCF/capex/FCF was USD 23.103B/28.499B/-5.396B; OCF included USD 11.363B of customer-prepayment financing component, and net ATM proceeds were USD 19.909B.
  • FY2026 Q4 RPO was USD 638B, up 363% year over year and USD 85B sequentially.
  • Q4 OCI/IaaS revenue was USD 5.787B, up 93% year over year; FY2026 OCI/IaaS revenue was USD 18.101B, up 77%.
  • FY2026 capex was USD 55.663B, FCF was USD -23.686B, borrowings were USD 129.541B, and cash/securities were USD 31.894B.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text: • FY2027 revenue guidance is at least USD 90B; it remains forward-looking. The Q1 ATM financing is completed rather than planned.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: Contracted demand at this scale can support power, facility, interconnect, cooling, and storage procurement. Supplier share, timing, and margin still require company-specific order evidence.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text: RPO is not all AI, near-term, or high-margin revenue. Customer prepayments are not revenue, 850MW is not proven full-load IT capacity, and capex/capacity does not identify a particular equipment beneficiary.

docs.title: Value capture and misread boundary
docs.text: Oracle's advantage is its database/application installed base, multicloud connections, and large OCI contracts. The market already sees the demand; the open question is RPO conversion, capacity delivery, and financed returns.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• RPO grows while IaaS revenue conversion keeps slowing.
  • Capex and financing rise without improvement in operating margin, FCF, or leverage.
  • OCF depends on large financing-component customer prepayments while delivery, revenue, and margin fail to convert in step.
  • Power, GPU, network, or construction delays block contracted capacity.
  • Large contracts are renegotiated, cancelled, or carry poor pricing/mix.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text:
ORCL is a Core / Market-found demand entity and capex-spillover validator. Q1 provides the first operating bridge between capacity delivery and OCI growth, while prepayments, negative FCF, and ATM financing leave return-on-capital proof open.

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: PDF Solutions mainly sells the analytics, connectivity, and process-control software layer for fab + assembly + test. Its AI relevance comes from the data-management and yield-improvement complexity of advanced packaging and test, not from any physical-equipment node.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: PDFS primary-owns the yield / process-control analytics data layer inside Semiconductor Manufacturing, Advanced Packaging, Test, and Materials. It is not a bonder, substrate supplier, inspection tool, or OSAT-capacity owner; it provides the software, connectivity, and analysis layer that stitches together fab, assembly, test, and backend equipment data.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: As advanced packaging and test become more complex, data standardization, yield analysis, and process control become more valuable. PDFS's current revenue bridge comes from Exensio usage in Intel AP&T and OSAT settings, CIM300 backend connectivity, and a business scale already visible in Q1 2026 revenue, margins, and backlog.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Q1 2026 quarterly total revenues were $60.1m, up 26% YoY; GAAP gross margin was 72%, non-GAAP gross margin was 76%; GAAP operating margin was 10%, non-GAAP operating margin was 25%; ending backlog was $246.4m.
  • The Intel page is explicitly titled Leveraging PDF Exensio for Intel Advanced Packaging and Test and says advanced packaging / testing creates major data-standardization and analysis challenges; Intel uses Exensio to manage and analyze manufacturing data from wafer fabrication to final testing.
  • Exensio OSAT is explicitly for Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test companies and includes process control, test operations, and assembly operations.
  • Exensio platform text says it spans fabrication, testing, assembly, and enterprise processes and states 55,000+ fab tools connected, 40,000+ process tools under process control, and customers across 350 organizations / 20 countries.
  • CIM300 explicitly says GEM300 standards can be adopted on semiconductor backend equipment, including packaging assembly and test equipment, even when the substrate is not a wafer.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text: • The Intel use case, OSAT positioning, and platform-scale metrics all come from issuer / product-page language; they prove product presence and routing but not a separate advanced-packaging / test revenue split by themselves.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: PDFS is a beneficiary of advanced packaging / test yield and process-control analytics, but the page only stays clean if it keeps the “data layer, not physical equipment” boundary explicit. It currently looks former-half-hidden: no longer totally overlooked, but also not one of the most crowded first-line hardware bottlenecks.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• AP&T / OSAT revenue mix is not separately disclosed.
  • Intel revenue contribution, customer concentration, and the share of backlog tied specifically to packaging / test are not disclosed.
  • It is not proven that PDFS should be written as a hardware bottleneck owner inside advanced packaging.

docs.title: Operating and capital delta as of 2026-10-04
docs.text:
This section supersedes older “current/latest” framing. Reported results and management guidance not yet replaced by results remain period evidence and testable gates; an August issuance date alone does not make a still-future guide obsolete.

PDFS’s Q2 USD61.5m revenue and USD270.7m backlog growth are positive facts, but sequential platform-revenue decline, volume-based revenue growth, USD14.1m capex, and a 1.9m-share secondary show that backlog is not common-owner cash. The 10.70x FY2025-sales screen requires recurring platform revenue and CFO to keep growing after dilution.

This round’s economic classification is Group 3 (not worth adding now). This page adds no price band, sizing, or execution trigger; What Is Worth Buying owns the four-group judgment and 大仓确认：NO remains in force.

docs.text:
Updated: 2026-09-09

Action route: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger currently selects none for PLUG; there is no current action or fallback.

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Plug Power sells fuel-cell systems, hydrogen supply, and related infrastructure capabilities. In this wiki it is not an ordinary data-center onsite-power company; it is a special case for whether hydrogen-product relevance can convert into data-center revenue before capital-structure stress overwhelms the path.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text:
• Lane: the hydrogen-optionality branch of spine 7, Onsite Bridge Power, Storage, and Backup
  • Boundary: this page only covers generation products, fuel supply, and time-to-power realization constraints
  • It does not own site switchgear, rack power, cooling, EPC/MEP, or any spine-8 infrastructure delivery in Facility Electrical, Rack Power, Cooling, and Delivery

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text:
• Realized results: the local filing and product materials show that the company explicitly treats data-center power as an application path and has a corresponding high-power fuel-cell platform.
  • Forward path: the AI/data-center narrative reaches realization only if issuer disclosure converts that application path into named projects, repeat orders, verifiable revenue/backlog, and sustainable unit economics.
  • Current conclusion: the existing filing does not break data-center activity into auditable commercial results, and capital-structure pressure remains the dominant constraint.

docs.title: 2026-08-10 Q2 update
docs.text:
• Q2 2026 revenue was about USD 178M, and gross margin improved to approximately breakeven from about -31% a year earlier. Net cash usage was about USD 61M, down about 58% sequentially.
  • Cash and cash equivalents were about USD 162M; total cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash were USD 671.5M. The issuer raised FY2026 revenue-growth guidance to 15%-16% and reiterated a Q4 positive-EBITDAS target.
  • The subsequent USD 80M Graham/electricity-rights transaction is a liquidity event. It does not establish data-center recurring revenue, durable unit economics, or a resolved capital structure.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Filing / issuer-primary: the Q1 2026 Form 10-Q and FY2025 annual filing define the current disclosure boundary.
  • Product / commercial materials: the GenSure HP launch and electricity-rights monetization materials show the product path and asset actions behind the hydrogen-power narrative.
  • Conclusion: the evidence currently reaches application direction and product preparedness, not data-center commercial revenue with healthy economics.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text: Company materials identify data-center power as a target application and present platform and asset actions intended to support that path.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: That is enough to keep PLUG in the hydrogen / capital-structure special-situation bucket, but not enough to restore it to the ordinary onsite-power ranking.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• Named data-center projects with realized revenue or backlog
  • Repeat-deployment economics, gross profit, or operating performance
  • A sustainable business path that no longer depends on recurring financing support

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• If later issuer evidence still stops at application language without data-center commercial realization, PLUG remains context-only and does not re-enter the ordinary ranking
  • If capital-structure or operating stress overwhelms product optionality to the point that the path is no longer realistically executable, it can leave ongoing spine-7 maintenance

docs.title: POWL — Powell Industries
docs.text: Action route: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger currently selects none for POWL; there is no current action or fallback.

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Powell owns medium-voltage switchgear and in-site power distribution within E8, taking power that has already reached the site and routing, protecting, and distributing it to critical loads inside the campus.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: POWL's primary lane is medium-voltage switchgear, site power distribution, power control rooms, e-houses, and integrated power packages. It is the owner of in-campus power distribution and control equipment; it does not own utility interconnection or substation EPC, it does not own rack-side UPS or thermal infrastructure, and it does not own upstream generation and fuel assets or server and networking-system manufacturing.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: After external power reaches an AI campus, it still has to be safely distributed to buildings, modules, and critical loads. Powell monetizes the layer where power is on site but not yet reliably distributed across the campus through switchgear, distribution systems, PCR and e-house products, and integrated power packages.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• The Q1 FY2026 results raw file explicitly discloses data-center orders well in excess of USD 100M, including a megaproject booking of about USD 75M, proving the company has won real datacenter electrical-delivery demand.
  • The Integrated Package Solutions product page shows Powell is not just selling a single cabinet; it also offers power control rooms, e-houses, and more integrated in-site distribution solutions.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• Company framing presents datacenter orders, integrated package solutions, and more complex electrical-delivery requirements as growth drivers.
  • The current local issuer and product evidence supports Powell's effort to expand through higher-spec electrical packaging, but that remains issuer framing rather than a disclosed long-duration AI revenue structure.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• If AI campuses keep scaling in size and load density, the content per project for in-site medium-voltage distribution, protection, and modular electrical rooms should rise, making Powell's revenue bridge broader than standalone switchgear.
  • POWL is distinctive because it sits after the utility handoff and before rack and facility thermal infrastructure, owning the middle layer where in-site distribution actually has to get built.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• The current local evidence does not show a durable revenue and margin conversion path from datacenter orders, and it does not prove that this order intensity will persist.
  • The current local evidence does not support Powell owning utility interconnection or substation EPC, or rack-side power and thermal infrastructure; those remain separate owners.

docs.title: Q3 FY2026 result — order proof upgraded, call pending
docs.text:
• The official release reported Q3 revenue of USD 312M / +9%, gross margin of 30.6%, and diluted EPS of USD 1.42; the upgrade is concentrated in the order and backlog evidence rather than an unqualified earnings beat.
  • New orders were USD 934M / +158%, about 3.0x book-to-bill, and backlog was USD 2.4B / +69%, including a data-center mega order above USD 400M. The order is tied to a behind-the-meter on-site-generation design, strengthening proof at the E8 site-distribution/custom-package layer.
  • The Q1 and Q3 SEC acceptance-time proxies both sit about 18.5 hours before the next-day 11:00 ET call. That is established after-close-release / next-morning-call cadence, not an unusual Q3 delay. SEC acceptance is a filing-time proxy, the issuer gave no scheduling rationale, and Q3 call/Q&A had not occurred at the 2026-08-04 14:39 CEST research cutoff.
  • The 2026-08-04 07:12 CEST Futu capture reported after-hours USD 188.2224, overnight USD 189.98, and bid/ask USD 188.10/189.00. These were thin extended-hours indications, recorded alongside the completed-session snapshot and the 200D 191.2044; they do not establish regular-session liquidity or delivery economics.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• If later disclosure shows datacenter orders are not converting into sustained in-site distribution revenue, or integrated packages are not increasing content per project, the E8 owner thesis weakens.
  • If execution remains too project-custom and value capture stays thin, Powell's stability inside E8 declines.
  • If the page starts extending Powell into utility-interconnection ownership, upstream generation and fuel ownership, or rack-thermal ownership without local-source support, that is a kill signal.

The Q3 large order and backlog prove demand, but roughly 54% conversion, customer/cancellation terms, normalized margin and cash conversion remain open; the 30.6% margin containing closeouts/contract liabilities is not extrapolable. Conditional watch pending those items and same-date valuation.

docs.title: PSIX — Power Solutions International
docs.text: Updated: 2026-09-09 CEST Industry page: Onsite Bridge Power, Storage, and Backup

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Power Solutions International's core business is natural-gas / diesel gensets and power systems. It sells onsite generation and standby equipment, not utility-generation asset ownership.

docs.title: 2026-08-06 Q2 earnings update
docs.text:
• Q2 net sales were USD 152.5M, down 21% year over year, and diluted EPS was USD 0.73. The company attributed lower sales to Power Systems shipment timing and softer oil/gas demand.
  • Management said data-center power-solutions demand remains strong, reduced total debt by about USD 30.8M, and expects second-half sales to exceed first-half sales.
  • Order timing, data-center shipment conversion, and the durability of margin improvement remain open.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text:
• It belongs to the Phase 5 E7 onsite / bridge generation and backup-equipment segment inside the generation / grid / time-to-power causal lane.
  • The role boundary stops at genset and power-systems supply. It does not extend into site electrical distribution, rack power, cooling, or EPC spine 8.
  • PSIX is a bridge / backup equipment mechanism, not a utility-generation owner and not a proven AI pure play.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: If a data center, campus, or supporting utility needs power before permanent supply is fully ready, PSIX can turn that time-to-power need into revenue through gensets, power systems, and after-sales support. That path depends on orders, shipment timing, and project cadence; it is not a durable AI annuity by default.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• The local power-systems capture explicitly lists DATA CENTER and UTILITY among the end markets.
  • Local results and call captures include direct management references to data-center demand or data-center applications.
  • The local 10-K capture is enough to establish that the company sells engines and power-systems equipment, not an abstract theme proxy.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• The company places data-center demand inside the demand stack for the power-systems business.
  • Company materials position PSIX as a supplier that can provide faster onsite or standby power capability.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• PSIX belongs on the active Phase 5 E7 list because the product mechanism clearly sits in the onsite / bridge generation and backup lane.
  • But this page is about a high-volatility equipment supplier, not about a proven owner of stable AI economics.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• The page does not have named hyperscaler deployment evidence or repeatable data-center order proof.
  • The page does not isolate AI-only revenue, AI-only backlog, or data-center-only service revenue.
  • The page also does not prove that this revenue path is durable enough to classify PSIX as an AI pure play.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• If future issuer-primary or filing evidence stops naming data centers as an end market or demand driver for power systems, this page's role should be downgraded.
  • If data-center-linked orders fail to turn into repeat shipments, revenue, or service evidence, the AI-to-revenue logic should be rewritten.
  • If the business mix shifts back toward generic industrial or oil-and-gas volatility rather than time-to-power / standby use cases, this page should leave mainline tracking.

docs.text: Quanta Services owns utility interconnection, substation, and site-power EPC delivery inside E8, engineering available power from the outside network into a deliverable datacenter site.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: PWR's primary lane is utility, interconnection, substation, and EPC delivery across transmission and distribution, substations, and large-load-center electrical infrastructure. Its ownership is outside-network-to-site power delivery execution rather than equipment content; it does not own upstream generation and fuel assets, it does not own a medium-voltage switchgear equipment platform, it does not own rack and facility power plus thermal infrastructure, and it does not own server or networking-system manufacturing.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: Before a rack can be energized, an AI campus has to solve interconnection, expansion, substation work, line work, and site electrical delivery. Quanta monetizes that layer through utility work, substation work, large-load-center electrical construction, and commissioning, with revenue conversion tied to project execution milestones rather than standalone equipment shipments.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• The FY2025 10-K and the Q1 2026 10-Q explicitly cover electric power transmission and distribution, substations, and infrastructure services for large load centers including data centers and advanced manufacturing.
  • Company filings place data centers, technology-related dynamics, electrification, and utility demand in the same demand frame, proving Quanta already sits in the execution layer of AI-campus power delivery.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• Issuer framing treats electric-infrastructure demand, large-load-center buildout, and related delivery work as future growth sources.
  • The local evidence supports management's view that datacenter demand and broader grid buildout are linked demand drivers, but that is still a workload and backlog framing rather than a disclosed AI revenue breakout.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• If hyperscaler and colocation campuses need faster interconnection, substation expansion, and site delivery, an execution platform like PWR should benefit directly from higher engineering complexity and tighter schedules.
  • PWR's E8 role is to convert utility-side readiness into a deliverable site, not to own upstream power supply itself and not to own downstream equipment content.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• The current local evidence does not isolate AI-related engineering revenue, and it does not prove that datacenter work will have structurally better economics than the broader utility and industrial EPC mix.
  • The current local evidence does not support Quanta owning generation and fuel assets, a medium-voltage switchgear platform, or rack and facility thermal infrastructure; those remain separate owners.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• If later disclosure shows datacenter and large-load-center work is not converting into sustained engineering revenue or execution quality, the E8 owner thesis weakens.
  • If utility and interconnection work proves to be only a small cyclical slice rather than a stable datacenter-delivery layer, the current page boundary should be rewritten.
  • If the page starts describing PWR as a generation-asset owner, an in-site distribution equipment owner, or a rack-thermal owner without local-source support, that is a kill signal.

docs.text: Qualcomm earns from handset/PC/automotive/IoT chipsets, connectivity platforms, and technology licensing. Its main AI mechanism remains low-power on-device/edge/physical AI. AI200/AI250, HUMAIN, and the named multi-generation Amazon custom-silicon/optical route make data-center opportunity more tangible but not yet core reportable revenue.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: QCOM is edge/physical-AI architecture context in Semiconductors and Foundational Compute, with secondary networking/connectivity. It is not an NVDA/AVGO-level data-center core or a foundry owner. Amazon, Alphawave, and wired connectivity expand customer/capability evidence but do not prove scaled custom-silicon monetization.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: On-device AI can increase premium SoC/NPU, automotive/robotics platform, and license value. Data-center monetization requires actual AI200/AI250 rack or custom-silicon shipments, customer deployment, and repeat orders. Handsets, QTL licensing, mix, and R&D still dominate economics.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• The latest captured quarter, Q3 FY2026, reported revenue of USD 9.947B, down 4%, and GAAP/non-GAAP EPS of USD 1.87/2.21, down 23%/20%.
  • Q2 10-Q Automotive revenue of USD 1.326B/+38%, IoT revenue of USD 1.726B/+9%, and nonreportable revenue/EBT loss of USD 141M/-121M remain a historical mix baseline, not the current quarter.
  • A September 8 8-K disclosed an Amazon warrant for up to 25.0M shares at USD 161.26, expiring 2036-09-03. The first 3.75M vested on initial purchase commitments; later tranches link to commercial arrangements, binding purchase orders, and actual purchases.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text: Qualcomm and Amazon describe multi-generation custom AI-inference silicon plus optical connectivity up to 1.6T, SerDes, and optical DSP. The USD 60B figure is the payment ceiling for full warrant vesting, not a firm order, backlog, revenue, or shipment disclosure; margin and repeatability remain unreported.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: Low-power compute, connectivity, and automotive/robotics distribution give Qualcomm a distinct route into physical AI and edge inference.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text: AI200/HUMAIN targets and the Amazon payment ceiling are not production revenue, and not all automotive/IoT growth is AI. No specific PO, shipment, revenue, margin, or deployment volume is disclosed, and the documents do not show that Amazon is replacing AVGO.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• Handset/QTL economics weaken faster than diversification grows.
  • Data-center shipments slip or fail to show a named customer, revenue, margin, and repeat order.
  • Edge/physical-AI products do not increase measurable content or royalty economics.
  • R&D and acquisitions fail to convert into FCF and per-share growth.

docs.title: 2026-07-29 latest captured earnings baseline — not valuation
docs.text:
• Fiscal Q3 2026 revenue was USD 9.947B, down 4% YoY, and non-GAAP EPS was USD 2.21, down 20%; memory/supply cost pressure was a real operating drag.
  • Management expects non-handset revenue, including Data Center, to accelerate from +24% in FY2026 to >60% in FY2027, while Modular adds an open foundation for generative and agentic AI.

docs.title: 2026-09-16 Amazon custom-silicon delta
docs.text: Amazon makes the custom-inference customer route named and upgrades QCOM from broad optionality to a revenue-proof-gated AVGO comparator. The warrant aligns future purchases with potential equity dilution, but vested shares are not exercised shares and cashless exercise makes actual dilution unknown. Remaining gates are binding PO disclosure, shipments, revenue, margin, deployment, repeat orders, and economics after warrant consideration.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: QCOM is Context / Bridge / Benchmark, primarily edge/physical AI; data center is now a named but revenue-proof-gated AVGO competitive check. All old tactical price bands have been removed from the current evidence chain. The registry remains none, and this page creates no numeric action or sizing authority. Large-position confirmation: NO.

docs.title: RMBS — Rambus
docs.text: Role: spine 3 memory-interface chips / controller IP / CXL Structural status: active Formal discovery state: Market-found Workflow modifier: former-half-hidden Evidence through: 2026-08-19; action SOT: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger, whose memory/storage row is none with no fallback.

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Rambus earns from memory-interface chips, silicon-IP licensing, and contract revenue. It does not make HBM/DRAM; it supplies controllers, interfaces, and connectivity between processor and memory. Existing DDR5-related product revenue is financial, while HBM4E/CXL remains more forward-looking.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: RMBS primary-owns the interface/controller/IP node in Memory, Storage, and In-System Data Movement. MU owns physical memory and NVDA/AMD compute architecture. Rambus connects them without owning either. Enterprise data/context software remains in spine 9.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: Higher bandwidth and channel count can raise interface-chip volume, content, and IP-license opportunities. Production products create product revenue; IP/design wins monetize through license, royalty, or contract. Standards, qualification, mix, and repeat wins determine value.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Q1 2026 GAAP revenue was USD 180.2M; product revenue was USD 88.0M, up 15%.
  • Licensing billings were USD 70.8M; operating cash flow was USD 83.2M.
  • Q2 FY2026 GAAP revenue was USD 207.385M; product revenue was USD 99.154M, royalties USD 84.261M, and licensing billings USD 84.1M.
  • Quarter-end Q2 AR was USD 144.094M and inventory USD 74.836M. The two largest customers represented 22% and 16% of Q2 revenue, and two customers represented 42% and 23% of quarter-end AR.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text: Rambus guided Q3 total/product revenue to USD 210-216M / USD 110-116M and explicitly conditioned achievement in part on signing customer agreements for product sales and solutions licensing. Public primary evidence through the cutoff does not establish that the Q3-required agreements were signed. That is publicly unproven, not a claim that they were not signed. LPDDR5X SOCAMM2, HBM4E controller IP, CXL, and PCIe 7 are product-direction evidence, not production share or attributable revenue.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: A tighter bandwidth bottleneck can increase controller/interface complexity and monetizable IP value, making Rambus closer to data movement than generic AI adjacency.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text: HBM4E/CXL/PCIe optionality is not current revenue. Q3 agreement signing, named or quantified design wins, share, royalty rate, and production timing are not disclosed facts.

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Sanmina is an electronics-manufacturing and complex-systems delivery company. For spine 6, the most relevant piece is the Communications Networks and Cloud & AI Infrastructure bucket together with the acquired ZT Systems manufacturing capability. Its official capability pages also cover optical/RF/microelectronics, PCB, backplane, cable, rack integration, and test.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: In spine 6, SANM is a manufacturing/integration exposure, with the most direct handle coming from ZT-enabled cloud-rack and cluster-scale AI manufacturing. It is not a branded systems vendor and must not be treated as a pure optical/DCI name. It belongs to the same manufacturing-conversion layer as CLS and FN, but customer and product boundaries differ.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text:
• Q2 FY2026 net sales were USD 4.013B; Communications Networks and Cloud and AI Infrastructure revenue was USD 2.771B, up about 278% year over year and about 69% of total sales.
  • For H1 FY2026, the same bucket generated USD 4.735B, up about 222% year over year. The 10-Q says the increase was primarily driven by the cloud-infrastructure end market, the ZT acquisition, new program wins, and related ramp-ups.
  • The Q2 FY2026 SEC/IR primary capture（源文件保留在私有研究库） records ZT Systems revenue of USD 1.88B, about 46.9% of quarterly revenue; it also lists product examples including 400G/800G/1.6T optical systems and pluggables, accelerated-compute GPU, storage, and IP switching/routing.
  • Q3 FY2026 net sales were USD 3.464016B. The reported combined Communications Networks and Cloud & AI Infrastructure end-market bucket was USD 2.148413B, or 62.02% of revenue. It is a combined bucket, not pure Cloud/AI revenue and not optical/DCI revenue.
  • The Q3 10-Q discloses ZT Systems revenue of about USD 1.1B in Q3 and about USD 4.0B since acquisition. Because ZT is integrated into ongoing operations, standalone profitability is not determinable.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Q2 FY2026 and H1 FY2026 revenue, growth, and mix for Communications Networks and Cloud and AI Infrastructure have been disclosed.
  • The 10-Q and issuer capture state that growth in this bucket was primarily driven by the cloud-infrastructure end market, the ZT acquisition, and new program wins.
  • Q3 combined end-market revenue, ZT revenue, and consolidated margin/cash flow have been disclosed; they do not provide standalone ZT margin, FCF, or optical revenue.
  • The AMD/ZT transaction materials state that Sanmina became AMD's preferred NPI manufacturing partner for cloud rack and cluster-scale AI solutions; ZT is described as a manufacturer of AI and general-purpose computer infrastructure for hyperscale computing companies.
  • Official capability pages support optical/RF/microelectronics, high-speed PCB/backplane/cable, rack integration, and test capability.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• Product examples and capability pages show what Sanmina wants to serve, but capability descriptions are not standalone proof of revenue realization.
  • The preferred NPI manufacturing partner wording proves positioning in the relationship, not an automatic long-term large-scale revenue commitment.
  • Management said core Sanmina and ZT secured more customer orders, but it did not disclose order dollars, backlog, duration, named customers, acceptance milestones, or attributable revenue. This remains an issuer statement, not a quantified orders-to-revenue bridge.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• SANM's most credible AI monetization path is cloud-rack and cluster-scale manufacturing rather than a fully proven optical/DCI revenue story.
  • Optical, backplane, cable, and test capabilities show that SANM can participate in more complex networking/interconnect manufacturing content, but that eligibility cannot be written up as material optical revenue.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• That material AI optical/DCI revenue has formed a separately visible revenue pool.
  • Named hyperscaler, network-OEM, or optical-customer revenue beyond the AMD/ZT language.
  • Standalone ZT margin, FCF, cash-cycle contribution, or integration completion.
  • That optical/RF/microelectronics mix has been proven to sustain higher consolidated margins.

docs.text:

SANM’s Q3 core Sanmina USD2.4bn, ZT USD1.1bn, and Cloud & AI bucket prove rack manufacturing, but the combined bucket is not pure AI/optics and ZT has no standalone margin/FCF/cash-cycle. docs.text: Updated: 2026-09-09 CEST Industry page: Platform Technology, Internet, and Distribution Classification: commerce infrastructure

docs.title: Theme position
docs.text: Merchant operating system, payments and merchant services, and unified online/offline commerce infrastructure.

docs.title: Why it is in this theme
docs.text: Shopify is more than an online-store builder. Q1 2026 GMV exceeded USD 100B, and merchant-solutions revenue was materially larger than subscription-solutions revenue, showing the business expanding from software subscriptions into transactions, payments, credit, and commerce infrastructure.

docs.title: My current preferred bullish case
docs.text: Q1 2026 GMV was USD 100.743B; revenue was USD 3.170B, up 34% year over year; gross profit was USD 1.546B; operating income was USD 382M; and FCF was USD 476M, a 15% margin. The 2026-08-05 Q2 update strengthened the quality evidence: GMV, revenue, gross profit, and FCF all grew by more than 30%; revenue reached USD 3.583B, FCF reached USD 654M, FCF margin was 18%, and the Q3 outlook still called for low-thirties revenue growth.

docs.title: My current key risks
docs.text: Q2 transaction and loan loss provision was USD 94M, so merchant-credit and macro pressure still need continued validation. Better operating evidence makes the commerce-infrastructure thesis more durable; it does not show that the shares are attractive at any given price. Valuation remains a separate judgment.
