docs.title: SMHN — SUSS MicroTec
docs.text: Role: spine 5 manufacturing / packaging / test / materials active; temporary bonding / debonding / hybrid bonding equipment Structural status: active Formal discovery state: Research-seed Evidence through: 2026-10-07; action SOT: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: SUSS MicroTec mainly makes money from advanced-backend bonding equipment, especially temporary bonding / debonding and hybrid bonding. Its AI relevance comes from HBM and AI chip modules raising demand for those backend steps, but that logic still needs to be re-underwritten at a finer customer, product, and economics level.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: SMHN primary-owns the temporary bonding / debonding / hybrid bonding equipment node inside Semiconductor Manufacturing, Advanced Packaging, Test, and Materials. It is not an OSAT capacity platform, not analytics software, and not a test-interface platform; it expresses a narrower and more process-specific advanced-backend step.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: If HBM and AI chip modules keep scaling, wafer thinning, temporary bonding / debonding, and die-to-wafer hybrid bonding demand should expand with backend process intensity. SUSS's current revenue bridge first shows up in order intake, order book, and Advanced Backend Solutions scale rather than in separately disclosed AI / HBM revenue.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Q1 2026 order intake reached EUR 149.3m, up 69.5% YoY; SUSS explicitly said the driver was higher demand from key customers for solutions used in the value chain for AI chip modules.
  • Q1 2026 sales were EUR 86.5m, gross margin was 36.1%, EBIT margin was 4.3%, and the order book increased to EUR 330.1m from EUR 266.8m at 2025 year-end.
  • FY2025 sales were EUR 503.2m; Advanced Backend Solutions revenue was EUR 349.7m, up 10.7%.
  • XBC300 Gen2 D2W is described as a fully automated solution for sequential die-to-wafer hybrid bonding on 200mm and 300mm substrates.
  • The 2023 HBM / AI temporary-bonding release explicitly said AI chips combine logic with HBM, that temporary bonding / debonding is indispensable for HBM thinning and downstream processing, and that SUSS temporary bonding is used by one of the world's leading foundries in advanced packaging.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• 2026 guidance points to a slight sales decline and a lower EBIT margin; that is forward-looking management guidance rather than delivered evidence.
  • “Key customers,” “leading foundry,” and the AI-chip-module value-chain wording are issuer statements and should not be upgraded into named-customer monetization proof.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: SUSS is a narrow expression of an advanced-backend equipment step and proves that bonding / debonding / hybrid bonding is not just a story. But the page still carries a re-underwrite modifier because “AI chip modules demand” is not yet the same thing as durable, separable AI / HBM monetization.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• Named AI / HBM customers are not disclosed, and AI / HBM revenue mix is not separately disclosed.
  • Advanced Backend Solutions is not the same thing as total advanced-packaging / hybrid-bonding economics.
  • The proof that still needs re-underwriting is customer concentration, the real order mix tied to hybrid bonding / temporary bonding, the conversion of order book into profit, and whether demand persists beyond a single program cycle.

docs.title: Operating and capital delta as of 2026-10-07
docs.text:
H1 revenue202.8m/EBIT14.2m(7.0%), orders410.0m/book473.7m. ABS orders326.2m include imaging/coating/bonding, not pure TBDB/HBM revenue. The115m Taiwanese advanced-packaging order is200/300mm spin coaters; no Micron link is verified. H1 bonding revenue declined and high-margin temporary-bonder mix fell, so the large order is not automatically high-margin revenue.220m scheduled for FY27 is delivery timing only.

FCF16.4m accompanies33.8m higher contract liabilities. Net cash63.6m still requires lease/other-liability distinctions.300m convert/warrant and about10% conditional capital are unused authorization, not actual dilution. Retain conditional Group2: convert425–485m revenue/35–37%GM/8–10%EBIT to cash; November5 Q3 is the next actual checkpoint. Quantified product/order/cash evidence can suffice; named customers are not the sole gate. MU expansion is an industry read-through, not a company order. What Is Worth Buying; large-position confirmation:NO (大仓确认:NO).

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• The AI chip module demand wording disappears or order growth resets sharply.
  • Advanced Backend Solutions keeps scaling without comparable improvement in profit quality or moat.
  • Hybrid bonding / temporary bonding remains demo-scale or overly dependent on one customer.
  • Weak guidance turns out to be structural rather than timing-related.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: SMHN is an Active / Research-seed advanced-backend equipment name with a re-underwrite workflow modifier. To move it higher, the advanced-packaging proof needs to be rebuilt at the product, mix, margin, and cash-conversion level rather than staying at order-language plus broad backend scale.

docs.title: SMTC Semtech
docs.text: Role: spine 4 optical/copper Signal Integrity modifier Structural status: active Formal discovery state: Market-found Modifier: former-half-hidden Evidence through: 2026-08-25

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Semtech earns from Signal Integrity, Analog Mixed Signal and Wireless, and IoT Systems and Connectivity. Its AI relevance is concentrated in Signal Integrity optical/copper interconnect, while the broader company remains a mixed analog and connectivity platform.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: SMTC primary-owns the high-speed signal-integrity node in AI Interconnect, Optical Networking, and DCI. It is not a module OEM or systems vendor, and its mixed-signal, wireless, and IoT businesses sit outside this page’s primary lane; those edges belong in cross-links such as Semiconductors and Foundational Compute.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: If data-center customers buy CopperEdge, FiberEdge, DirectEdge, CDRs, TIAs, drivers, and equalizers, the economics first appear in the Signal Integrity segment. Whether that becomes high-quality AI revenue depends on segment growth, margin, customer proof, and product attribution, not just “800G / 1.6T / 3.2T” marketing language.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• FY2026 Signal Integrity net sales were USD 322.608M, up about 23% from FY2025 USD 261.747M and about 82% above FY2024 USD 177.033M.
  • FY2026 Signal Integrity gross margin was 65.2%; Q4 FY2026 Signal Integrity net sales were USD 90.7M with 67.4% segment gross margin.
  • In the quarter ended 2026-04-26, Signal Integrity net sales were USD 102.003M with 62.7% segment gross margin.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• Official materials describe Signal Integrity as an optical/copper data-communications portfolio and position advanced CDRs, copper equalizers, optical solutions, CopperEdge, FiberEdge, and DirectEdge for 800G/1.6T and future use cases; these remain product-positioning claims.
  • Management positions Semtech for the 800G, 1.6T, and 3.2T buildout and says it continues to invest in next-generation optical and copper interconnect technologies.
  • Product pages and press releases frame the 224Gbps family, CopperEdge, FiberEdge, and DirectEdge for AI/ML clusters, hyperscale data centers, cloud infrastructure, and LRO/LPO/XPO/NPO/CPO use cases.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: If Signal Integrity keeps outgrowing the rest of the company, Semtech can keep rerating as a data-center interconnect modifier rather than only a mixed analog / IoT name.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• Named hyperscaler or NVIDIA revenue is not proven.
  • Named module-vendor volume awards are not proven.
  • CopperEdge / FiberEdge revenue split or a quantified multi-customer production ramp is not proven.
  • A product roadmap does not by itself prove durable high-quality AI revenue.

docs.title: Operating and capital delta as of 2026-10-04
docs.text:
This section supersedes older “current/latest” framing. Reported results and management guidance not yet replaced by results remain period evidence and testable gates; an August issuance date alone does not make a still-future guide obsolete.

SMTC’s Q2 FY2027 USD341.9m revenue, USD126.2m Signal Integrity at 65.3% GM, and USD68.9m CFO are positive facts, but GAAP EPS of USD1.59 includes a USD101.4m tax benefit and USD204.1m cash sits against USD492.8m debt. The 17.29x FY2026-sales screen requires Q3 guidance to become CFO under normal tax and debt/cash conditions.

This round’s economic classification is Group 3 (not worth adding now). This page adds no price band, sizing, or execution trigger; What Is Worth Buying owns the four-group judgment and 大仓确认：NO remains in force.

docs.title: 2026-08-25 Q2 FY2027 earnings update (historical disclosure; current framing is updated by the 2026-10-04 delta)
docs.text:
• Q2 net sales were USD 341.9M, non-GAAP EPS USD 0.71, and operating cash flow/free cash flow USD 68.9M/61.4M.
  • Signal Integrity net sales were USD 126.2M and segment gross margin 65.3%. Q3 guidance was net sales of USD 410M +/- USD 5M and adjusted EPS of USD 1.05 +/- USD 0.03.
  • The release reports accelerating bookings and record backlog but does not quantify CopperEdge, FiberEdge, DirectEdge, customer/module-vendor awards, or hyperscaler revenue. The GAAP net-income line includes a USD 101.4M tax benefit.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• CopperEdge disclosure / litigation risk worsens.
  • Signal Integrity growth or margin weakens materially and stops proving segment importance.
  • The company cannot quantify any durable AI / data-center revenue bridge or customer adoption.
  • Competitors suppress Semtech’s share in the same interconnect / signal-chain budget.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text:
SMTC is a positive partial proof Signal Integrity modifier. Q2 strengthens segment revenue, margin, and guidance evidence while customer/product revenue attribution, litigation/control-risk detail, and official Q&A remain open.

Current action is routed only by Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger; SMTC is currently none, with no fallback.

docs.title: SNDK — Sandisk
docs.text: Role: spine 3 data-center flash / NAND storage Structural status: active Formal discovery state: Market-found Evidence through: 2026-10-07

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Sandisk earns from NAND flash, data-center/enterprise storage, and consumer/edge products, relying on its manufacturing JV with Kioxia. AI data growth raises demand for higher-value flash, while NAND pricing, customer commitments, and manufacturing economics remain cyclical.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: SNDK is the data-center flash/capacity-performance node in Memory, Storage, and In-System Data Movement. It differs from MU HBM/DRAM, WDC capacity HDD, and RMBS interface/IP. Enterprise data/context platforms such as SNOW are not physical storage.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: Training/inference data, checkpoints, and high-performance datasets raise data-center flash volume and mix, monetized through products and multi-year commitments. NAND ASP, cost per bit, contract pricing/guarantees, concentration, and JV capex determine profit.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Q3 FY2026 revenue was USD 5.95B, up 97% sequentially and 251% year over year.
  • Data-center revenue was USD 1.467B, up 233% sequentially and 645% year over year.
  • Sandisk ended Q3 with three signed New Business Model agreements and signed two more in Q4.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text: The company calls this a fundamental inflection and describes firm financial commitments in multi-year engagements. Prior Q4 revenue guidance of USD 7.75-8.25B is superseded by the August 5 Q4 actual results above; contract quality, pricing and cash conversion remain research questions.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: Higher data-center mix and multi-year contracts may reduce spot-NAND volatility without eliminating supply/pricing cycles.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text: Backlog/guarantee figures from a third-party transcript are not verified by the local issuer capture and are not treated as facts. Signed agreements do not automatically prove high margin, low concentration, or non-cancellability.

docs.title: Operating and capital delta as of 2026-10-07
docs.text:
FY26 revenue20.248B/adjusted EPS70.88. CFO11.671B less direct capex0.177B gives11.494B; subtract JV net cash0.275B and NBM prepayment/deposit effect2.476B for adjusted FCF8.743B. Low direct capex does not remove Kioxia JV funding/commitments. Only19% of59.8B RPO is expected within12 months. Refundable customer deposits1.5B are not permanent cash.

Eight-customer NBMs cover about half of FY27 bits/two-thirds of FY28, improving price/volume/cash visibility without a group profit floor. Investor-Day FY28–30 targets of roughly80%GM/75%OP/50% adjusted FCF margin are targets, not guidance; delivery-case models are not conservative bases. Move ordinary-add research to Group1 with lower confidence than MU and material exit/cycle/cash sensitivity. Dated judgment: What Is Worth Buying. Registry=none; large-position confirmation:NO (大仓确认:NO).

docs.title: 2026-08-05 Q4 FY2026 earnings update
docs.text:
• Q4 revenue was USD 8.97B, up 51% sequentially. FY2026 revenue was USD 20.25B, up 175% year over year, and Datacenter revenue grew 437%.
  • The board approved an additional USD 14B buyback, leaving USD 15.5B authorized. Q1 FY2027 revenue guidance was USD 10.30B-10.80B and non-GAAP EPS guidance USD 44-46.
  • NAND pricing, New Business Model contract quality, customer concentration, and cycle durability remain open.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• Data-center revenue/contract conversion slows or concentration and renegotiation rise.
  • NAND supply expansion and falling ASP erode gross margin.
  • JV capex, yield, or technology transitions weaken cash and cost position.
  • Strong guidance fails to become FCF and durable per-share earnings.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text:
SNDK is an Active / Market-found data-center-flash entity, beyond the old “only NAND cycle/spin” label but still constrained by cycle and contract quality.

docs.title: SNOW — Snowflake
docs.text: Role: E9 data-plane governed cloud data / AI platform owner Structural status: core Formal discovery state: Market-found Evidence through: 2026-10-04. FY27 Q2 (July 31 period end, September 2 release) is the operating baseline; Q1 raw remains historical comparison only. Action routing: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger.

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Snowflake is a governed cloud data platform for enterprise data and AI workloads. Its stable ownership sits at the unified layer for storage, governance, sharing, analytics, and AI capability access, not at the application-owner layer and not in hardware, systems, or physical infrastructure.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: SNOW sits in the E9 data plane across Platform Technology, Internet, and Distribution and AI Application Production and Data Lifecycle. It owns the Data Cloud, Cortex, Snowflake Intelligence, and the consumption platform around enterprise data governance, but it does not absorb application owners, cloud hardware, E2 silicon, E6 systems, or E7/E8 physical infrastructure.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: Snowflake's AI-related revenue does not come from a broad AI company narrative. It comes from product consumption on top of the existing data platform: customers keep, govern, and operate data inside Snowflake, then call storage, compute, sharing, Cortex, and AI capabilities. The real proof is whether workload usage, retention, RPO, and AI-capability adoption remain durable.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Q2 FY2027 product revenue was USD 1.4919B, up 37%; total revenue was USD 1.546793B, up 35%. RPO was USD 9.0B/+30%, NRR 126%, and million-dollar customers 828/+27%.
  • GAAP product gross margin was 70.9% versus 74.7% non-GAAP. GAAP operating loss of USD 263.0M must remain separate from non-GAAP operating profit of USD 237.0M.
  • H1 operating cash of USD 334.580M less USD 18.005M capex gives USD 316.575M FCF, against USD 826.052M SBC. SBC is not a current cash payment, but equity compensation is an economic cost. Do not annualize Q2 FCF.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• FY27 product-revenue guidance rose from USD 5.84B to USD 6.07B, with 14.5% non-GAAP operating margin and 23% adjusted FCF margin. These are forecasts, not realized AI revenue or common-shareholder cash returns.
  • Management attributed roughly half of the growth acceleration to AI products, not half of group revenue. Lower-margin AI workloads also reduced the product-margin outlook; usage, revenue and profit must be checked together.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• AI-capability account counts are not paid revenue, and the issuer does not allocate every dollar of growth by product. That disclosure limit neither invalidates realized group product revenue nor independently rules out investment.
  • The priced USD3.75B 0% notes comprise USD2.0B due 2029 and USD1.75B due 2031. Expected net proceeds are USD3.70B, with planned uses of USD383.5M for capped calls and USD548.3M to retire USD261.8M of old principal. Gross principal is not automatic incremental dilution, and financing cash is not operating cash. The closing 8-K remains inaccessible to root in this run; completion date and actual post-close balances are unverified, a verification limitation rather than issuer nondisclosure or a failed closing.
  • July cash, the September 2 FY27 380M diluted-share assumption and later financing are not a same-date EV bridge. Independently of closing status, the disclosed sales valuation and SBC support no-add.

docs.title: Cash and current-valuation boundary
docs.text: The October 2 regular close was USD 341.04. Price times the pre-financing FY27 380M diluted-share assumption divided by guided product revenue of USD 6.07B gives a 21.35x price/product-sales proxy, not actual current market capitalization or EV/total sales. Operating acceleration is confirmed, but the 21.35x guide-product-sales proxy and Q2 SBC at 28.39% of product revenue require more return delivery than lower-multiple, GAAP-profitable cash-generating alternatives. Group 3: not worth adding currently, not because standalone AI revenue is missing or closing is unverified. Reassess if two further reports sustain product growth while reducing the SBC burden, or valuation falls materially. Large-position confirmation: NO. The consolidated judgment belongs in What Is Worth Buying. SNOW is outside CRM/NOW/TEAM/APP action coverage and inherits none of their price bands.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: Snowflake's scarcity comes from enterprise data governance, cross-cloud sharing, and keeping analytics plus AI usage inside one governed platform. The misread boundary is turning it into an application owner, a generic software seat story, or a hardware / physical-buildout owner. It owns the data plane, not the endpoints or the physical stack.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• If retention, RPO, million-dollar customers, and AI-capability adoption start diverging, the data-plane monetization case needs to be re-underwritten.
  • Product costs persistently outgrowing revenue, SBC/financing dilution offsetting cash improvement, or valuation depending on unsustainable growth would weaken expected per-share returns.
  • If AI capabilities remain enablement without sustained product consumption, the thesis strength is overstated.
  • If later local source work no longer supports the governed cloud data / AI platform role, this page should contract.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: SNOW is Core / Market-found. Its stable E9 ownership is the governed cloud data / AI platform and does not extend into application owners, E2 silicon, E6 systems, or E7/E8 physical infrastructure. Any current action lives only in Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger.

docs.text: Role: E10 cross-theme digital-bank, lending, and financial-services platform Structural status: active Formal discovery state: Market-found Updated: 2026-07-13; action SOT: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: SoFi combines a member entry point, lending, financial-services products, and the external-client Galileo technology platform. Core revenue still comes from spread, fees, and platform/service economics rather than a standalone AI revenue line.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: SOFI belongs to the E10 cross-theme fintech portfolio, not a tenth AI or data-center supply spine. It owns the digital-bank, lending, and financial-services-platform role. It does not absorb HOOD's retail-brokerage and crypto entry point, AFRM's BNPL merchant network, or a generic application or physical-infrastructure role.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: AI is currently a support layer inside loan-application workflow and service productivity. If it improves underwriting, document handling, service efficiency, or user experience, value must still show up through conversion, credit outcomes, cost efficiency, spread, fees, or platform revenue. AI is not separately disclosed as revenue.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Official IR materials and the Q1 FY2026 8-K describe SoFi as a member-centric one-stop digital financial-services platform with lending, financial-services, and technology-platform segments.
  • The Q1 FY2026 packet records member/product, origination, loan-platform, lending net-interest-income, and brokerage-fee anchors. These are broad financial-services actuals, not AI-attributed revenue.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• The company describes Personal Loan Doc Coach as an AI-powered tool inside the loan-application workflow.
  • That product framing proves AI has entered the service workflow, not standalone AI monetization.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• If AI-assisted workflow shortens application and service cycles and improves underwriting consistency, SoFi may benefit through conversion, cost, and credit outcomes.
  • Wider external Galileo use could add platform revenue that differs from balance-sheet spread economics.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• AI has created separately trackable revenue, ARR, or profit contribution.
  • Broad member, product, origination, or lending growth is directly attributable to AI.
  • SOFI should absorb HOOD, AFRM, or a wider application or infrastructure-owner role.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• If credit performance or funding costs deteriorate, member and origination growth may not become durable earnings.
  • If external Galileo growth stalls, SoFi will remain more dependent on balance-sheet spread and the consumer-credit cycle.
  • If AI tools produce no verifiable conversion, cost, credit, or paid result, this page should keep AI as a support layer.

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Teradyne makes money from semiconductor test platforms. Its AI relevance is real because HBM, chiplets, and 2.5D / 3D packages increase memory-test, thermal-aware-test, and known-good-everything complexity, but it is still a broad ATE platform rather than an advanced-packaging owner.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: TER is only a test-infrastructure benchmark inside Semiconductor Manufacturing, Advanced Packaging, Test, and Materials. It does not own the packaging-equipment node or the materials / purity node; this page exists to benchmark narrower names such as FORM, SMHN, and PDFS rather than to promote TER as the primary execution name.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: As AI chips move from monolithic die to chiplets, HBM, and larger advanced packages, testing expands beyond a single die toward die, bridge, interposer, substrate, and stack validation. Teradyne's revenue bridge comes from higher memory / compute test intensity, not from packaging capacity itself.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Q4 2025 results were above the high end of guidance, and management explicitly said growth was fueled by AI-related demand in compute, networking, and memory within Semi Test.
  • Teradyne's technical article explicitly said the industry has entered the era of heterogeneous chiplets in advanced integrated packages, where AI packages combine CPUs, GPUs, and HBM in a single advanced package.
  • The same article directly connected CoWoS, 2.5D / 3D packaging, large CoW modules, thermal dissipation, and rising test complexity.
  • The article also extended the test problem from known-good-die to known-good-interposer and known-good-CoW style validation.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• Q1 2026 guidance was revenue of USD 1.15B-1.25B; that remains forward-looking guidance rather than delivered evidence.
  • Management expects year-over-year growth across all businesses in 2026, with strong momentum in compute driven by AI; that is forward-looking outlook rather than a proven revenue split.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: TER proves that AI / HBM / chiplet complexity raises the value of test infrastructure, but it is best used as a benchmark-only ATE platform. Writing it as the owner of the advanced-packaging lane would blur platform test exposure with packaging-node ownership.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• HBM-related test revenue is not separately disclosed.
  • The advanced-packaging share of revenue is not separately disclosed.
  • It is not proven that TER should primary-own the spine 5 packaging lane.

docs.title: Operating and capital delta as of 2026-10-04
docs.text:
This section supersedes older “current/latest” framing. Reported results and management guidance not yet replaced by results remain period evidence and testable gates; an August issuance date alone does not make a still-future guide obsolete.

TER’s Q2 USD1.329bn revenue, USD1.122bn Semi Test, and record Memory revenue confirm an ATE/memory benchmark, but HBM/advanced packaging has no separate revenue or cash disclosure. Delete the old quarterly-annualized sales multiple; retain the USD1.2–1.3bn Q3 guide as a issued management guide that remains a demand gate, not advanced-packaging owner cash.

This round’s economic classification is Group 4: key evidence insufficient, no add for now. This page adds no price band, sizing, or execution trigger; What Is Worth Buying owns the four-group judgment and 大仓确认：NO remains in force.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• AI stops showing up as a direct Semi Test demand driver.
  • Higher test complexity fails to translate into better business quality or higher value capture.
  • TER trades more like undifferentiated broad ATE beta and loses its usefulness as a benchmark reference.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: TER is a Context / Market-found ATE benchmark-only name. It stays in the wiki to calibrate the upper bound and maturity of the test layer, not to be upgraded into the primary advanced-packaging execution name.

docs.title: TLN — Talen Energy
docs.text:
Role: Phase 5 E7 spine 7 generation / grid / time-to-power; TLN owns dispatchable generation and campus power contracting Structural status: core Formal discovery state: Market-found Evidence through: 2026-08-05

Action route: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger selects VST, CEG, and TLN Current Live Research Conclusion as TLN's sole current SOT; this entity carries no price bands, position sizing, or trade instruction.

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Talen is an independent power producer centered on PJM. It owns Susquehanna nuclear generation plus gas and other dispatchable assets, and it earns through wholesale energy, capacity, ancillary services, and long-term power contracts.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: Within Power Generation, Grid, and Fuel Supply, TLN primary-owns dispatchable generation and campus power contracting. It owns site-level generation, PJM energy/capacity monetization, and campus-power contracts such as AWS. Its ownership stops at the site / utility handoff; inside-the-fence switchgear, UPS, cooling, and server / network layers do not belong here.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: TLN's cleanest AI monetization path is to bind Susquehanna's nuclear output to long-duration contracts for an adjacent data-center campus, then use PJM dispatchable assets and added capacity to backstop delivery. The monetized layer is site-level electricity, capacity, and contractual delivery, not data-center internal infrastructure.

docs.title: 2026-08-05 Q2 update
docs.text:
• Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA was USD 374M and adjusted free cash flow was USD 212M.
  • The company raised 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to USD 2.025B-2.225B and adjusted free-cash-flow guidance to USD 1.200B-1.350B. These guide figures do not make total generation earnings AI-specific.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• The 2025 annual report disclosed about 13.1 GW of power infrastructure, including about 2.2 GW of nuclear generation, plus a meaningful dispatchable fossil fleet.

  • The Q1 2026 10-Q disclosed that the revised AWS PPA moved to a front-of-the-meter structure providing up to 1,920 MW through 2042; the transition to the revised structure occurred in April 2026.

  • The August 5 Q2 release confirms that Cornerstone closed in June 2026, adding about 2.6GW of generation, and cites a pipeline of about 4GW of land-development and data-center contracting options.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• The earlier Q1 full-year Adjusted EBITDA / Adjusted FCF guidance explicitly excluded Cornerstone. That is a historical pre-close basis and cannot automatically be applied to the raised August 5 guidance above.
  • Q1 2026 results and the April 2026 senior-notes release disclosed Cornerstone assets of Lawrenceburg 1,120 MW, Waterford 875 MW, and Darby 456 MW, or 2,451 MW total; these are pre-close asset/financing disclosures; the Q2 release confirms that closing occurred in June 2026.
  • The shareholder letter describes the expanded AWS PPA as roughly USD 18B of 17-year notional revenues and treats it as a base for further data-center contracting.
  • Management frames Freedom, Guernsey, and the Cornerstone assets as part of the Flywheel strategy to strengthen future campus / large-load contracting capability.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• TLN is one of the clearest cases of a single nuclear campus directly tied to AI power demand, which makes the ownership very pure but also concentrates the risk in Susquehanna, AWS, and PJM / FERC rules.
  • Added and acquired gas assets make TLN look more like a dispatchable platform that can backstop long-duration contracts, rather than only a single nuclear-asset story.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• The full AWS ramp schedule, post-close Cornerstone integration and economics, and TLN's ability to expand campus-power contracting beyond Susquehanna / AWS are not yet proven by reported results.
  • TLN's total PJM revenue base or total generation earnings should not be treated as equivalent to AI monetization.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• The AWS PPA's regulatory or contractual path is materially weakened, or the front-of-the-meter structure cannot advance as disclosed.
  • Susquehanna availability, licensing support, or safety / operating performance materially weaken long-duration delivery capability.
  • PJM / FERC large-load or co-location rule changes materially damage campus-power contracting economics.
  • Post-close Cornerstone integration or economics disappoint in a way that weakens TLN's dispatchable backstop and contracting capacity.

docs.title: 2026-10-04 frozen decision
docs.text:
Classification: Group 2 — reopen only after the stated valuation and operating conditions; no current add.

The September-29 USD1.5bn ASR initially delivers about 4.0m shares; final shares depend on VWAP and contractual adjustments, with settlement expected no later than Q1 2027, not a completed final share reduction. Approximately USD1.5bn of future PJM capacity revenue is monetized at SOFR+200bp. Issuer adjusted-FCF forecasts for 2H26–2028 are about USD4.0bn before and USD2.8bn after monetization; do not capitalize the same cash twice. At the 2026-10-02 USD320.77 close, equity/TTM sales was 4.11x. Final ASR shares, liabilities/future cash and the 2H27 3.5x leverage target remain proof gates; buyback size alone does not justify an add.

docs.title: Why it belongs in this theme
docs.text: Its core business remains vehicles and energy storage, but official filings have already positioned FSD, Robotaxi, Optimus, Cortex, and energy software as core technology pathways, so I view it as best monitored under conditional classification.

docs.title: My currently more credible bullish case
docs.text: Energy storage is becoming a second growth leg, and if autonomy and Robotaxi deliver, Tesla can move from a manufacturing story toward a software/platform valuation framework.

docs.title: My current top risks
docs.text: Automotive margins and delivery cadence still determine current cash flow; misalignment between autonomous-driving timelines, regulation, and valuation expectations can be very painful.

docs.title: 2026-10-04 current conclusion
docs.text:
TSLA generated H1 2026 CFO of USD8.634bn and cash capex of USD8.282bn, leaving USD0.352bn before finance leases. USD10.951bn is investing cash use, not capex; shares rose from 3.751bn in December 2025 to 3.949bn. Q2 deliveries of 480,126 and 13.5GWh of storage deployments are scale, not owner cash. Four-group result: 3 (not worth adding now); large-position confirmation: NO.

For the current-add conclusion, see What Is Worth Buying. Action remains only with the unique SOT selected by Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger; a none row has no fallback, and this entity does not copy numeric zones or sizing.

docs.text: Last updated: 2026-07-13 CEST

docs.title: Current role
docs.text:
• Structural status: core
  • Current role: Market-found
  • Primary lane: spine 5 foundry / process manufacturing anchor
  • Boundary: owns leading-edge logic, wafer manufacturing, and related advanced-packaging platform entry points; does not own the GPU / CPU / ASIC architecture narrative
  • Action pointer: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger

docs.title: Business and lane position
docs.text: In the local issuer raw, TSMC defines itself as a dedicated IC foundry and groups logic technology, manufacturing, 3DFabric, and advanced packaging inside one manufacturing-service stack. The durable AI framing here is manufacturing ownership: leading-edge logic nodes, wafer production, and related manufacturing services. This page does not treat TSM as a chip-design or architecture beneficiary.

docs.title: AI to revenue
docs.text: The local issuer/product raw does not disclose a standalone AI revenue ratio. The cleaner transmission path is that AI/HPC demand first lifts leading-edge node demand, wafer-capacity needs, manufacturing yield, and related packaging-service attachment, which then feeds foundry revenue and utilization. This page stops at that manufacturing transmission.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• The company defines itself as a dedicated IC foundry and discloses world's largest logic capacity of more than 17 million 12-inch-equivalent wafers in 2025.
  • The logic technology page says N2 started volume production in 4Q25 as planned, N3 entered high-volume production, and N5 serves smartphone and HPC applications.
  • The issuer raw also lists 3DFabric and advanced packaging service entry points, showing that advanced packaging is part of the manufacturing-service stack.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• The company presents A14 as a technology intended to drive AI transformation.
  • Deeper AI upside, customer mix, and profit contribution from 3DFabric / advanced packaging remain mostly at the capability-presentation level in the current local raw.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: • As long as AI accelerators continue to depend on the most advanced logic and associated packaging flows, TSM benefits as the manufacturing platform rather than as an architecture narrative.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• AI revenue share.
  • A standalone advanced-packaging profit pool, customer allocation, or near-term supply tightness conclusion.

docs.title: Operating and capital delta as of 2026-10-04
docs.text:
This section supersedes older “current/latest” framing. Reported results and management guidance not yet replaced by results remain period evidence and testable gates; an August issuance date alone does not make a still-future guide obsolete.

TSM’s CoWoS/advanced-node anchor role and full official Q&A are confirmed, but advanced-packaging capacity is not a standalone revenue stream. On the explicit 1 ADS = 5 ordinary-share basis, the 20.03x equity/sales screen on FY2025 USD122.42bn sales requires orders to become revenue/margin/cash under disciplined capex; do not add ADR and Taiwan ordinary-share market values together.

This round’s economic classification is Group 2 (consider an addition only after the stated operating and valuation conditions close). This page adds no price band, sizing, or execution trigger; What Is Worth Buying owns the four-group judgment and 大仓确认：NO remains in force.

docs.text:

  • Leading-edge demand no longer converts into manufacturing utilization, capacity realization, or customer adoption.
  • The page drifts back into treating TSM as a chip-architecture or design beneficiary.

docs.title: In plain language

Data-center demand can raise content, but TXN is not a GPU, custom XPU, or AI-network platform; industrial/automotive cycles and 300mm manufacturing economics matter more.

docs.title: Lane and boundary

Internal 300mm manufacturing is a cost/supply capability, not an advanced-logic foundry/package thesis.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: More server/data-center equipment can raise power-management, signal-chain, and control content through unit volume and content per system. Because TXN does not disclose AI revenue, data-center mix, margin, FCF, and cycle durability must validate value capture indirectly.

docs.title: Proven

docs.title: Issuer claim

docs.text:
Role: E10 cross-theme portfolio prose; AI/ML lending marketplace and funding-sensitive credit platform owner Structural status: active Formal discovery state: Market-found Evidence as of: 2026-08-04

Action route: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger currently selects none for UPST; there is no current action or fallback.

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Upstart's stable position is an AI/ML-driven consumer-credit matching and underwriting platform. The point here is not a broad fintech narrative, but whether model-driven approvals, bank partnerships, and funding recovery can keep converting into platform volume and revenue.

docs.title: 2026-08-04 Q2 update
docs.text:
• Q2 2026 total revenue was USD 365M, up 42% year over year; fee revenue was USD 348M, up 45%. Unsecured-lending fee revenue was USD 326M, and contribution profit was USD 201M at a 62% contribution margin.
  • Secured-products contribution margin improved to negative 35%, from negative 176% a year earlier and negative 96% in Q1. The company kept its full-year 2026 total-revenue expectation around USD 1.4B.
  • Funding-partner appetite, credit performance, and model trust still determine whether the reported recovery is durable.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: UPST sits on the fintech / consumer-credit side of E10 cross-theme portfolio prose. Its stable ownership is the AI/ML lending marketplace and funding-sensitive credit platform. It does not absorb PGY's B2B credit-decisioning / securitization infrastructure, KLAR's BNPL / digital-bank / merchant-consumer network, or PDD's commerce / application-owner role.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: Upstart's AI relevance comes from model-driven underwriting, pricing, and borrower / funding matching, not from broad fintech totals. This page only treats AI relevance as revenue-relevant when issuer / SEC evidence keeps tying model capability to originations, conversion, automation, or platform-fee revenue. Funding, credit, or total origination metrics do not automatically equal AI proof.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text: • Local issuer source defines Upstart as an AI lending marketplace connecting borrowers with banks and credit unions.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• The Fortress forward-flow announcement is a future funding arrangement announced by the company. It supports the funding-sensitive platform framing but is not realized proof before executed volume appears.
  • Company framing continues to center AI-enabled underwriting, loan matching, and bank-partnership expansion.
  • That framing proves business positioning, but it does not by itself prove AI as a separately monetized revenue line.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• If funding supply improves and partner acceptance of model performance holds, Upstart's platform volume, fee generation, and operating leverage can recover.
  • That recovery belongs first to credit-marketplace execution, not to merchant-network, commerce-traffic, or generic infrastructure ownership.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• The current local source set does not isolate AI revenue.
  • Broad origination, funding volume, or credit metrics are not automatic proof of AI monetization.

docs.title: Value capture and boundary of misread
docs.text: Upstart captures value by using models and workflow to improve credit underwriting and matching, then embedding that capability into banks, credit unions, and capital supply. The misread boundary is turning it into broader consumer-finance infrastructure, a merchant network, or an ecommerce / application platform. UPST owns the AI/ML lending-marketplace role here; it is not a substitute for other finance, commerce, application, or infrastructure owners.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• If funding-partner appetite contracts again, platform volume and profit elasticity get hit first.
  • If credit performance or model trust no longer sustains partner acceptance, the AI framing weakens into a normal cyclical credit platform.
  • If later local issuer / SEC evidence falls back to broad lending totals without more specific automation, approval, or conversion proof, this page should narrow its AI-relevance language.

Q2 revenue, fee revenue and contribution profit are positive operating proof; secured margin remains negative, funding/bank channels and credit-cycle risk remain to be validated, alongside same-date valuation. Conditional watch.

docs.title: Chain position
docs.text: Card network operator, global payments network, cross-border settlement, and value-added services platform.

docs.title: Why it is on this chain
docs.text: Issuer disclosures define Visa as a payment network and value-added-services platform, with economics distinct from a consumer lender.

docs.title: My current preferred bullish case
docs.text:
Proven: FY26 Q3 ended June 30 produced net revenue $11.633B (+14%), GAAP EPS $2.97 (+10%) and non-GAAP EPS $3.32 (+11%). Payments volume rose 10%, cross-border volume excluding intra-Europe 12%, and processed transactions 10%.

Proven: quarterly repurchases were $4.9B at an average $330.71, with $28.4B authorization remaining. A historical corporate repurchase price is not an investor entry level; authorization is not executed buying.

Inference: consumption and cross-border flows support network fees, while client incentives and bargaining determine net revenue and per-share cash.

docs.title: Cash and return underwriting — 2026-10-07
docs.text:
FY26 nine months plus residual FY25 Q4 derive TTM GAAP/adjusted EPS11.76/12.77 and CFO less capex21.013B; neither is issuer-reported TTM or unconditionally normalized cash. June30 net debt is about9.916B, not net cash. Nine-month buybacks/dividends20.282B exceed CFO16.342B. Net-share reduction is inside EPS growth, with no second buyback uplift. Q3 incentives were28.7% of pre-incentive revenue; the9M rate was broadly stable. Cross-border volume grew12% while international-transaction revenue grew6%; volume is not mechanically earnings.

Ordinary-add support depends on the return hurdle: the analyst three-year base including dividends is about9.3%, acceptable around9%; a10% hurdle favors a better price or stronger per-share growth evidence. The next earnings report is not a rigid permission gate. Litigation, settlement guarantees, incentives and cash conversion retain valuation discounts. Stablecoin/agentic products have no disclosed financial contribution and receive no option value. Groups and technical context: What Is Worth Buying. Large-position confirmation:NO (大仓确认:NO).

docs.title: My current key risks
docs.text: Antitrust, fee regulation, large-client bargaining and incentives can constrain monetization. Volume growth that fails to become net revenue and cash would weaken the toll-network case. Visa is not primarily a consumer lender, but that does not mean zero settlement or counterparty risk.

docs.title: One-line view
docs.text: FY26 Q3 validates volume and revenue growth; business quality does not automatically make the current valuation attractive. See What Is Worth Buying; actions route only through Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger. Large-position confirmation: NO.

docs.title: VICR — Vicor
docs.text: Updated: 2026-07-13 Industry page: AI Interconnect, Optical Networking, and DCI State: context / Needs-source

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Vicor belongs here as E8 high-density power module context, not as the owner-level benchmark for the whole AI power chain: the local packet proves a real product position in 48V/54V distribution, BCM, and dense near-load power, but it does not support treating Vicor as an owner of E7 generation, E2 compute silicon, or E6 systems, and it does not close AI revenue into durable proof.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: Vicor sits in the high-density power-module and near-load conversion layer where facility / rack-power hands off toward the accelerator. The local evidence supports roles in 800/400 VDC -> 54/50/48 V front-end step-down, 48V/54V distribution, BCM bus conversion, and current multiplication / power-on-package close to GPU or ASIC loads; it does not support claiming that Vicor owns every future AI rack-power architecture.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: The revenue chain only closes if AI racks keep or re-adopt the HVDC -> SELV 48/54 V -> near-load current multiplication stack, Vicor modules are designed into the platform, and those platform insertions convert into recurring production shipments. The current local evidence proves technical fit and issuer product positioning more than it proves broad AI production revenue.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text: Company product material, SEC filings, and local raw captures prove that Vicor has 48V/54V distribution, BCM, power-on-package, and other dense near-load power solutions for computing and data-center use, and that it presents those solutions against high-current accelerator power problems.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text: Issuer material places those modules inside the GPU / accelerator near-load power path and the high-voltage DC front-end step-down chain. That proves how the company describes its role, but it does not prove that future AI racks must keep the 48V/54V intermediate layer or that named-customer production attribution has closed.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: If AI racks end up standardizing on HVDC -> 48/54 V -> near-load current multiplication, Vicor can benefit as an E8 high-density power-module supplier. That is better preserved as context than as a benchmark-owner claim for the entire power chain.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text: The local packet does not yet prove that 48V/54V is the default next-gen AI rack standard, that Vicor has closed named hyperscaler or OEM production share, that its AI revenue mix is visible, or that AI deployment has already translated into durable margin structure improvement.

docs.title: Operating and capital delta as of 2026-10-04
docs.text:
This section supersedes older “current/latest” framing. Reported results and management guidance not yet replaced by results remain period evidence and testable gates; an August issuance date alone does not make a still-future guide obsolete.

VICR’s 48V/54V, BCM, and near-load module capability remains a valid architecture branch, but 800V-to-6V/12V paths can bypass the assumed 48V bottleneck. Without named platform production, revenue, margin, or cash, retain old technical-fit language as capability; architecture adoption cannot substitute for economic conversion.

This round’s economic classification is Group 3 (not worth adding now). This page adds no price band, sizing, or execution trigger; What Is Worth Buying owns the four-group judgment and 大仓确认：NO remains in force.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text: If later local evidence shows more AI racks bypassing the layer where Vicor sits, for example by moving more directly from 800 VDC to lower voltages without preserving a 48V/54V intermediate stage, this page should be downgraded further or removed from active context. As long as the proof remains technical and issuer-led rather than production and revenue-verified, the name must stay Needs-source.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: Context / Needs-source. The earlier benchmark-style treatment is retired here in favor of context: E8 role means high-density power modules at the facility / rack-power to near-load conversion boundary, not owners of E7 generation, E2 compute silicon, or E6 systems.

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Vertiv owns the last E8 stretch from in-building power and thermal infrastructure to an energized rack, turning site power into racks that can run reliably.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: VRT's primary lane is facility and white-space electrical plus thermal infrastructure: UPS, power distribution, busway, thermal management, liquid cooling, rack-side power, and service. The boundary starts inside the site and data hall and ends at the energized rack; it does not own utility interconnection, substations, or upstream generation and fuel assets, and it does not own servers, networking gear, or system manufacturing.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: AI training and inference raise rack power density, heat density, redundancy requirements, and deployment urgency at the same time. To turn site power into live compute, customers need more UPS, distribution paths, liquid cooling, thermal modules, and follow-on service work, which maps directly to Vertiv's products and solutions.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• The 2025 10-K and the Q1 2026 8-K define Vertiv as a critical digital infrastructure platform spanning power, cooling, IT infrastructure solutions, and services.
  • The Q1 2026 8-K shows data-center demand driving sales growth, with management explicitly tying customer demand to deployment speed, operational efficiency, and denser infrastructure.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• The 2025 shareholder letter and Q1 2026 8-K frame backlog, capacity expansion, strategic investment, and share gain as the main drivers of future growth.
  • The Ohio expansion release announces planned additional U.S. thermal-management manufacturing capacity for AI data centers; it is future capacity-investment and delivery-readiness framing, not proof that the added capacity is already operational.
  • Management presents faster deployment, higher reliability, integrated service capability, and liquid-cooling demand as the main bridge from AI buildout to future revenue conversion.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• If AI rack density keeps rising, site-level spend per campus on in-facility power, rack-side power, thermal management, and liquid cooling should rise as well, supporting higher content and service attach for Vertiv.
  • Because Vertiv sits on the final stretch from facility power to an energized rack, it is more directly exposed than upstream power-build or pure IT-hardware names to the question of how power actually becomes running compute inside the building.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• The current local evidence does not isolate a durable AI revenue percentage, and it does not prove that liquid cooling and high-density deployments will structurally lift margins over a longer cycle.
  • The current local evidence does not support Vertiv owning utility interconnection, substation build, or upstream power-supply assets; those remain separate owners.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• If later disclosures show that higher-density and liquid-cooling demand is not pulling through incremental power and thermal attach, or that backlog is mainly one-off project noise rather than repeatable platform demand, the E8 owner thesis weakens.
  • If site-level power and thermal content becomes standardized and heavily commoditized, revenue may grow while value capture shrinks.
  • If the narrative drifts into upstream generation, grid interconnection, or server-system manufacturing without source-backed proof, the page boundary should be rewritten.

Q2 sales were USD3.274bn, up 24%, adjusted operating margin 22.6%, adjusted EPS USD1.52 and adjusted FCF USD925m; FY adjusted-EPS guide is USD6.65-6.75. Supply congestion and multi-phase execution remain real risks; even strong operations leave no valuation margin of safety. Move to group 3 not worth adding currently / large-position NO and retire BUY/ranges.

docs.title: VST — Vistra
docs.text:
Role: Phase 5 E7 spine 7 generation / grid / time-to-power; VST owns merchant / retail generation plus capacity Structural status: core Formal discovery state: Market-found Evidence through: 2026-08-07

Action route: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger selects VST, CEG, and TLN Current Live Research Conclusion as VST's sole current SOT; this entity carries no price bands, position sizing, or trade instruction.

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Vistra is an integrated merchant-power and retail-electricity platform. It owns nuclear, natural-gas, coal, solar, and storage assets, then combines generation, retail sales, capacity, and hedging through a unified commercial platform.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: Within Power Generation, Grid, and Fuel Supply, VST primary-owns merchant / retail generation plus capacity. It owns the generation assets, retail platform, hedging/commercial stack, and long-term power contracts. Its ownership stops at the site / utility handoff; inside-the-fence switchgear, rack power, cooling, EPC, and server / network layers do not belong here.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: When hyperscalers or other large-load customers sign long-term power contracts, VST turns existing nuclear and gas assets into contracted energy, capacity, and attribute revenue, then uses its retail and commercial platform to manage delivery and risk. The monetized layer is power generation and sales, not internal data-center electrical buildout.

docs.title: 2026-08-07 Q2 official refresh
docs.text:
• Q2 2026 ongoing-operations adjusted EBITDA was USD 1.767B, more than 30% above the USD 1.349B prior-year figure. The company maintained 2026 ongoing-operations adjusted EBITDA guidance of USD 6.8B-7.6B and adjusted FCFbG guidance of USD 3.925B-4.725B.
  • GAAP Q2 net income was USD 305M and included a USD 472M unrealized hedge loss. The local Q2 evidence also adds Helix/NVIDIA/KKR/KIA and Cogentrix regulatory evidence, while potential Cogentrix and Meta PPA contributions remain excluded from the stated framework.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• 2025 results disclosed about 3,800 MW of nuclear PPAs, including the long-term AWS contract at Comanche Peak and the long-term Meta contracts across PJM nuclear assets.
  • Official Q1 2026 materials confirmed that Meta's 20-year PJM nuclear PPAs cover 2,609 MW.
  • The annual report shows that Vistra combines multi-region generation, retail electricity, and commercial risk management. This is a generation + retail platform, not a single-plant story.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• The company expects part of the Meta operating energy / capacity to begin delivery in late 2026, full operating delivery by year-end 2027, and uprate delivery across 2031-2034.
  • Management tied expected annual load growth of 5-6% in ERCOT and 2-3% in PJM directly to AWS / Meta PPAs and broader load growth.
  • Vistra announced a planned acquisition of about 5,500 MW of Cogentrix gas assets, but Q1 2026 guidance and the 2027 midpoint opportunity explicitly exclude the potential contribution from Cogentrix and the Meta PPAs.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• VST monetizes AI / data-center demand not because all revenue becomes AI revenue, but because it can translate nuclear, gas, and capacity ownership into steadier contracted cash flow through long-term contracts plus a retail/commercial platform.
  • Compared with a single-site story, Vistra looks more like a diversified power-supply platform with multiple assets and customer routes.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• The full Meta ramp, the realized benefit after Cogentrix closes, and the amount of incremental profit that data-center demand will ultimately retain inside Vistra are not yet proven by reported results.
  • Vistra's total revenue, retail revenue, or total generation earnings should not be broadly labeled as AI revenue.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• AWS or Meta contracts are materially weakened, canceled, or move materially off the disclosed delivery path.
  • Key nuclear or gas assets lose availability, licensing support, or commercial execution needed for long-duration delivery.
  • The retail and commercial platform stops converting large-load growth into lockable energy / capacity economics.
  • Later results show that data-center contracts are isolated events rather than durable platform cash-flow drivers.

USD1.5bn of subordinated notes due 2057 was issued on September 24: USD850m at 7.000% and USD650m at 7.250%. This is completed financing, not operating accretion or common-share dilution. Intended uses include later preferred redemptions, which were not established as completed at the cutoff. The 2026-10-02 close was USD140.02, with provider TTM/forward P/E of 23.9x/13.6x. Capital cost after preferred disposition, generation/hedging cash and capital returns remain conditions; old zones do not reactivate.

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Western Digital earns from high-capacity/nearline HDDs that store persistent data for hyperscale and enterprise customers. AI creates more warm/cold data and capacity demand, but HDD is not the primary real-time memory bottleneck. Capacity cost, qualification, pricing, and cash conversion drive value.

docs.title: Lane and boundary

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: Cloud/AI customers add persistent datasets, checkpoints, and archives, raising nearline exabytes, ASP, and higher-capacity mix. Revenue/margin depend on qualification, product transitions, supply discipline, and customer digestion rather than AI-data headlines alone.

• Fiscal Q4 revenue was USD 3.747B, up 44% year over year. GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins were 54.1% and 54.4%; cash flow from operations was USD 1.39B and free cash flow was USD 1.28B.
  • Q1 FY2027 guidance midpoint was approximately USD 4.1B of revenue, 55.5% non-GAAP gross margin, and USD 4.00 non-GAAP EPS. Capacity-storage demand and cash conversion are confirmed, while the cycle, ASP, and customer digestion remain evidence gates.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Q3 FY2026 revenue was USD 3.34B, up 45% year over year and 11% sequentially.
  • GAAP/non-GAAP gross margin was 50.2%/50.5%.
  • Operating cash flow was USD 1.12B; FCF was USD 978M.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text: WDC's prior Q4 guide midpoint of USD 3.65B revenue and 51.5% non-GAAP gross margin is superseded by the August 5 Q4 actual results above. Its claim that training, inference, agentic and physical AI data require persistent low-cost HDD storage, together with the 100TB+, High Bandwidth Drive and qualification roadmap, still needs shipment, customer-mix and cash evidence.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: AI data growth supports long-duration capacity demand, with HDD retaining a low-cost-per-TB role even when hot data uses flash.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text: Not all WDC growth is AI, and high gross margin cannot be perpetually extrapolated. AI data growth does not ensure continuous hyperscaler buying or permanent supply discipline.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• Hyperscaler digestion slows exabyte shipments, ASP, or revenue materially.
  • Capacity roadmap, yield, or qualification delays cost share.
  • Industry supply discipline breaks and gross margin/FCF falls rapidly.
  • Flash or architecture substitutes nearline workloads faster than expected.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: WDC is an Active / Market-found capacity-storage entity, not an HBM-like real-time compute bottleneck. Q4 proves financial monetization; historical market-action overlays do not belong on this page.

docs.title: SANM monitoring checklist
docs.text:
Current state: research-only proof watch / registry=none / no current action or numeric-zone authority. SANM cannot inherit this optics/DCI SOT; a historical remote stack exists, non-authoritative.

  • Keep USD 2.148413B / 62.02% as a combined Communications Networks and Cloud & AI Infrastructure end-market measure. Do not relabel it as pure AI or optical revenue.
  • Track ZT durability: Q3 ZT revenue is about USD 1.1B, but standalone margin, FCF, and cash-cycle contribution are not determinable after integration.
  • Track concentration: top-ten customers were 62% of Q3 sales and 67% for nine months; one Q3 customer represented at least 10% of revenue and one quarter-end customer at least 10% of gross AR.
  • Track cash quality: issuer-defined Q3 FCF was USD 23.685M versus OCF of USD 124.491M and USD 100.806M of PP&E purchases. Nine-month receivable sales of USD 486.745M rule out treating OCF alone as high-quality conversion.
  • Track leverage and working capital: cash USD 1.844942B, total term debt USD 2.172310B, and Q3 interest expense USD 32.464M; assess debt/interest, working capital, and contingent consideration together.
  • Require a disclosed program, customer, order, shipment, or revenue/margin bridge before treating optical systems/pluggables, high-speed backplanes, cables, or test systems as optical/DCI monetization.
  • Treat the 2026-08-18 close of USD 198.28 as a dated snapshot only. With registry=none and numeric authority=NO, do not state a price band or line action.

Upgrade requires ZT revenue durability together with margin proof, a combined-bucket increase that is not merely acquisition effect or a relabeling exercise, a quantified AI/networking order/revenue bridge or optical attribution, and no new concentration, receivable-sales, debt/interest, or cash-conversion break. Downgrade follows if ZT supplies revenue without margin/FCF, customer concentration or receivable-sales dependence worsens, leverage/interest pressure rises, or optical/DCI remains only a capability list.

docs.title: 2026-10-04 economic readback — no new bands
docs.text:
The 2026-09-08 action contract is unchanged and all six large-position confirmations remain NO; this review raises no band and performs no remote mutation. Completed-session prices in the 9/8 table are then-selected-SOT provenance, not 10/2 prices or automatic execution. Latest 2026-10-02 market references are Tencent HKD421.20, PDD ADS USD75.38, and Alibaba HKD104.40; they do not amend the contract or recalculate bands. Alibaba AI Cloud/Compute Services is paid segment revenue/EBITA, but capex was RMB67.678bn, company-defined FCF negative RMB44.670bn, and the 710m placement implies about 3.57% enlarged-share dilution; Tencent post-capex FCF was negative RMB13.8bn; PDD revenue/operating profit grew only 8% and ordinary-holder net income fell 12%; Baidu AI Cloud Infra growth does not replace an independent AI/cloud cash-return bridge. These facts strengthen proof/kill boundaries and do not expand the SOT's small-position/observation semantics into a new value judgment.## BABA 8/26 completed-placement per-share bridge

Alibaba completed the placement of 710m new ordinary shares at HKD112.70. The announcement states estimated net proceeds of approximately HKD79.7bn; its disclosed use-of-proceeds components are HKD47.871bn for global computing infrastructure plus HKD31.914bn for hyperscale data-center, cloud-storage, database, and network upgrades, totaling HKD79.785bn, which is the working input below. The August monthly return takes ordinary shares from 19,174,988,918 to 19,884,988,918.

Item Calculation Result Enlarged shares monthly return 19.884989bn Net cash / ordinary HKD79.785bn / 19.884989bn HKD4.012 Net cash / ADS (8 ordinary shares) HKD4.012 x 8 HKD32.099 Net cash / ADS at illustrative HKD7.80/USD 32.099 / 7.80 USD4.115 Constant-profit EPS pressure 19.174989 / 19.884989 - 1 -3.5705% 9/4 ADR close translated to ordinary at HKD7.80/USD 113.24 x 7.80 / 8 HKD110.409 Price versus placement 110.409 / 112.70 - 1 -2.03%

If profit were unchanged, the enlarged denominator lowers EPS by about 3.5705%. But net placement cash contributes about USD4.115/ADS to the per-share balance sheet, so the old band must not be mechanically cut by 3.7%. The cash is also earmarked for AI/cloud capacity while June-quarter FCF outflow was RMB44.670bn, so the band must not be mechanically raised by USD4.115. This is a pro forma comparison of June-quarter financials, the 8/26 placement, and the 9/4 market price, not a current-cash claim.

BABA action: USD97-118 remains a conditional observation range, pending deployment of placement cash, AI Cloud margin/FCF conversion, and the next diluted ADS/share-count bridge. There is no automatic starter permission inside it. The USD154-190 trim framework remains inherited discipline and is not raised here.

This page asks which next evidence could most change an industry judgment. docs.title: How the whole chain earns returns
docs.text:
flowchart TB
  D[Cloud and end-customer paid demand] --> C[Capital budgets and financing]
  C --> A[GPU/ASIC design]
  C --> E[Generation/grid/distribution/cooling/construction]
  A --> F[Advanced wafers and memory]
  W[Equipment/materials] --> F
  F --> P[Substrates/packaging/known-good dies/test]
  P --> R[Servers and racks]
  R --> O[Energization/commissioning/bandwidth/utilization]
  E --> O
  N[Copper/optics/networks] --> O
  T[NAND/HDD persistent storage] --> O
  O --> U[Cloud revenue and paid applications]
  U --> X[Operating cash returns after delivery]
  X --> D

These are parallel requirements. HBM expansion, substrate pricing, or a power agreement alone cannot make a cluster usable. Cloud capex and chip, wafer, memory, and server revenues repeatedly record the same spending along the chain; adding them does not produce an AI total market. Compare incremental profit, capital needs, and cash at each layer.

Industry judgment Beneficiary or constraint anchors Evidence and limits Largest separately reported data-center revenue platform NVDA FY27 Q2 DC revenue $89B; group OP $63.734B. DC is not exclusively AI, and group profit is not DC segment profit Memory is a separate, large profit pool MU, SK hynix, Samsung DS; SNDK/Kioxia for NAND MU FQ4 GAAP OP $43.751B; SKH Q2 OP KRW60.5426T; Samsung DS OP KRW89.2T. MU FQ4 has 14 weeks. Different periods, currencies and business scopes prevent a precise ranking; group profit is not HBM profit Manufacturing and packaging across GPU/ASIC architectures TSM; FORM, BESI, CAMT/ONTO by process TSM Q2 group GM 67.7%; packaging profit is not separately disclosed. Test, bonding, and inspection require their own order-to-revenue/cash evidence; process necessity alone does not prove pricing power Substrates have demonstrated scarcity-to-price-to-profit transmission Ibiden; Unimicron for product mix Ibiden's official Q&A attributes profit improvement primarily to pricing and identifies high-multilayer demand above supply. Unimicron ABF is 52% of product revenue, not market share. Easing material risk does not instantly create qualified substrate capacity Custom compute and networking have monetized AVGO, ANET; separate CRDO's AEC AVGO Q3 AI semiconductor revenue $16.7B; group FCF includes software. Over 90% of CRDO's revenue increase came from AEC, not an all-optical ramp InP is a local constraint supported by contracts AXTI; LITE/COHR customer checks Capacity reservations and contractual deposits are stronger than capability claims, but signing, receipt, good output, delivery, and revenue differ. This proves neither universal module scarcity nor an AXTI monopoly Deliverable power and systems have time value GEV, VRT, ETN; separate BE and contractors GEV's 53GW backlog and 63GW SRA are distinct; VRT Q2 adjusted OP margin 22.6%. Equipment output is not grid connection, and group profit is not AI project profit

System revenue does not imply equal profit capture. DELL's latest quarterly AI server revenue was about $16.4B, with reported FCF $0.986B versus adjusted FCF $8.149B; FN's annual FCF was $4.2M and SMCI's annual CFO -$6.810B. Receivable financing, leases, inventories, and customer advances explain how demand, profit, and shareholder cash can diverge.

MU's current attribution uses FQ4: DRAM revenue rose 27% sequentially with mid-single-digit bit and high-teens pricing growth; NAND rose 42%, with bits about +10% and prices about +30%. FY26 has 53 weeks and FQ4 14, so these are not constant-week growth measures. The 26 SCAs, approximately $150B minimum-price volume RPO and approximately $32B customer financial commitments are distinct contract measures, not one cash line. Annual deposit-financing inflow of $12.747B has occurred and is no longer described as expected in FQ4. It is outside OCF, subject to eventual conditional refunds, and unlike VRT operating deferred revenue. FY26 gross-spend cash arithmetic of $58.963B is distinct from company-adjusted FCF of $62.308B; fab spending and deposit refunds constrain common-shareholder cash.

September 10 conditional analysis is complete: price and volume protection has a term, and customer funding has financing value; neither alone identifies a group cash floor. Separate same-capacity protection and ceiling concessions from the total effect of contract-induced expansion, including investment, industry-price feedback and refunds. Two normally performing conditional scenarios produce opposite whole-cycle results; MU's actual path still requires the expiry ladder, investment rigidity, price-cost evidence and funding bridge. See Storage, Memory, and CPU-Adjacent Bottleneck Follow-up Tracking Ledger.

docs.title: Four priority research questions
docs.text:
Order Complete question and primary subject Current conclusion Evidence that could change the conclusion Stop or downgrade criteria 1 MU: which price/volume drivers produced exceptional memory profits, and how durable are they? SKH/Samsung checks High profits have materialized; assess effective HBM, conventional DRAM, and NAND supply separately rather than perpetuating current margins ASP/bits/mix, costs, qualified good output, customer inventory, capex, LTA terms, and mid-cycle profit Effective supply and customer inventories rise while ASP weakens; publicly unidentifiable product-profit attribution becomes an explicit disclosure limit 2 Ibiden: how durable is high-multilayer substrate pricing power? Unimicron price/mix, TSM/FORM process anchors Official evidence supports price-to-profit transmission; materials, labor, yields, and qualification constrain ramp timing Price/mix to OP to cash, actual output, ramp, and packaging/KGD alignment Supply exceeds demand, prices fall, customers dual-source, or expansion persistently fails to produce cash 3 AXTI: is scarcity and profit in InP, lasers, modules, or platforms? LITE/COHR and ANET/CRDO checks InP reservations raise research value; deliverable good output and unit economics remain decisive Actual deposit receipt/credits, effective capacity, export permits, yields, customer delivery, and margins Ramp delays, permits/second sourcing, refunds/contract concessions, or volume without better unit profit 4 ORCL: does energization constrain cloud revenue, and who captures time value? GEV/VRT delivery checks, MSFT cash comparison Cloud revenue is growing; RPO cannot substitute for capacity, financing, or project returns Q1 is published and checked; next-period capacity/OCI, advance-to-revenue conversion, capex/leases, funding and per-share cash; Point Beach approval Delayed deployment/procurement, conversion below commitments with worsening financing; RPO growth alone is not a rebuttal

ORCL's September 10 FY27 Q1 results and 10-Q have now been checked; they are no longer pending. The October 2 Point Beach arrangement is subject to regulatory approval: a conditional future energy commitment, not cash paid or a realized project return. Its approximately $300M must not be mechanically added to existing power/supply or lease obligations.

docs.title: Demand, cash, and falsifiable scenarios
docs.text:
MSFT's official call reported about 1GW added in the quarter, nearly halved dock-to-live time in major regions, and FY26 Q4 FCF of $19.6B. Deployment efficiency also creates usable supply. ORCL FY27 Q1 OCF of $23.103B includes $11.363B of additional customer prepayments with a significant financing component and $3.997B of other deferred revenue. Capex of $28.499B leaves FCF of -$5.396B. Approximately 141M issued shares produced $19.909B of net ATM financing, not operating cash. Reconcile $288B of uncommenced leases separately from $34.150B of supply/power obligations; do not add them as present-value debt.

Ibiden's JPY26.5B price/mix profit bridge is a full-year forecast revision versus May, not actual quarterly profit; Q1 CFO of JPY95.892B includes JPY73.575B of additional advances received. Third/fourth glass-cloth sources are candidates for mass-production use, not proof that every specification is qualified and shipping.

Separate advances: VRT Q2 deferred revenue increased $1.1715B, with a net $451M working-capital contribution; GEV H1 contract liabilities/current deferred income increased $13.695B. These accompany real operating growth and future delivery obligations. Do not annualize quarterly cash or claim that simply deducting every advance yields normalized FCF.

Scenario, without assigned probabilities Causal impact Common falsifier Paid demand persists and supply gradually expands Constraints migrate across memory, packaging, optics, and energization; firms retaining profit and post-delivery cash as output grows benefit Do utilization and paid revenue follow actual delivery? ASICs/inference efficiency alter unit content Manufacturing and delivery across architectures remain important, but memory, bandwidth, and GPU-hours per task change Does token growth offset declining resources and prices per task? Supply outruns demand or financing/ROI weakens Delays, inventories, lead times, and advances can deteriorate before profits; linked companies diverge at different times Do multiple demand anchors and supplier ASP/orders/working capital weaken together?

Phase 3 remains a demand falsification layer. CRM/APP test payment and cash, DOCN cloud capacity, and BLZE storage; NET/FSLY and other governance, security, and service names require distinct transmission mechanisms. DOCN's AI Customer ARR includes those customers' other cloud services, and committed MW is not live capacity. TASK AI Services grew about 26%, but group revenue only about 5% while adjusted EBITDA fell 11.2%: AI demand does not guarantee matching profit growth.

docs.text:

  • Read common quarterly indicators: payment/revenue, usable capacity, ASP/unit content, cancellations/inventory, yields/effective capacity, OP, clearly defined FCF, and debt/equity/advance funding. Stop repeating searches for unidentifiable product profit until new disclosure appears.

docs.text:
• Active research caps are 4 P0 and 8 P1 slots, with at most 2 concurrent satellite slots in total. The four priority research questions rank marginal research value, not automatic P0/P1 occupancy.

  • Active query navigation is the union of three controllers, the proof ledgers, and registry-selected action SOTs, capped at 24; it is not a count of every physical query file.
  • New research waves first enter raw evidence and dated packets. Only stable analytical changes enter an existing program/ledger/SOT; any new active query must absorb or explicitly supersede an existing same-program entrance before net growth.
  • Event/special pages require an expiry trigger and return to evidence/history after reviewed closure rather than indefinitely occupying an active slot.

Research resources remain focused on memory-profit durability, high-multilayer substrate pricing and cash, InP contract-to-delivery conversion, and energization-to-cloud revenue. Existing admission gates and workload caps are unchanged. Use What Is Worth Buying for capital-add judgments rather than inferring them from research priority.

ORCL's September 10 FY27 Q1 results and 10-Q have been published and read, not left as a pending event: OCF includes substantial customer prepayments, reported FCF remains negative after capex, and ATM issuance is financing. The October 2 Point Beach arrangement remains subject to regulatory approval; it is not cash already paid and cannot be mechanically added to existing power commitments or uncommenced leases. The next test is conversion of prepayments, financing, and construction into durable revenue and attributable shareholder cash, not waiting again for an earnings event that has occurred.
